title: حِكَايَةُ نُورِ الدِّينِ عَلِيِّ بْنِ الْفَضْلِ وَأَنِيسِ الْجَلِيسِ
titleEn: The Tailor's Tale ends; The Tale of the Two Viziers and Anīs al-Jalīs begins
part: Night 34 · The Tailor's Tale ends / The Two Viziers and Anīs al-Jalīs begins
source: William Hay Macnaghten, ed., The Alif Laila, or Book of the Thousand Nights and One Night, vol. 1, Calcutta 1839 (“Calcutta II”), printed pp. 276–283 (Night 34, continuing directly from nights-33), transcribed from the 300 ppi scan (archive.org aliflailaorbooko01macn) by the editors' own transcription. The edition prints the prose essentially unpointed: ALL VOCALIZATION (tashkīl) IS EDITORIAL — ours, not the edition's — and the alphabet button strips it back to the bare rasm exactly as Macnaghten prints it. Romanization is simplified IJMES. Spelling, including the edition's Middle Arabic forms and its occasional compositor's slips, is preserved unaltered; a few genuinely obscure or corrupt-looking forms are vocalized by evident sense and flagged in the notes rather than silently repaired. Read-aloud audio is a Modern Standard Arabic reading of this vocalised text, synthesized by machine, with word-by-word timing generated the same way.
about: Night 34 brings the barber before the king of China, where he revives the hunchback by drawing the fishbone from his throat; the king has the story written in gold, rewards the tailor, the Jew, the Christian and the Muslim, and makes the barber his boon companion. Shahrazād then begins the tale of the two viziers: at Basra the good vizier al-Faḍl ibn Khāqān buys the slave-girl Anīs al-Jalīs for the king, but his son Nūr al-Dīn ʿAlī falls into her arms in the baths-house, and the vizier fears the rival vizier al-Muʿīn ibn Sāwī. As with every printed edition of the Nights, this one belongs to the late Egyptian recension (ZER) — an eighteenth-century expansion padded out to a literal 1001 nights; no printed edition is a medieval text, and Macnaghten regularised the language here and there, so some Middle Arabic texture is a nineteenth-century retrofit.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا كَانَتِ اللَّيْلَةُ الرَّابِعَةُ وَالثَّلَٰثُونَ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā kānati al-laylatu al-rābiʿatu wa-al-thalāthūna
sentences.l: And when the night, the fourth and the thirty, came to be,
sentences.i: When the thirty-fourth night came,
sentences.n: The edition prints الثلثون without the alif of ثلاثون; it is vocalised as it stands, with the missing long ā marked by the dagger alif, and the tens in the nominative plural as printed.

sentences.t: قَالَتْ بَلَغَنِي أَيُّهَا الْمَلِكُ السَّعِيدُ أَنَّ مَلِكَ الصِّينِ قَالَ إِيتُونِي بِالْمُزَيِّنِ وَيَكُونُ سَبَبَ خَلَاصِكُمْ وَنَدْفِنُ هَذَا الْأَحْدَبَ فَإِنَّ لَهُ مِنْ أَمْسِ مَيِّتٌ وَنَعْمَلُ لَهُ ضَرِيحًا
sentences.tr: qālat balaghanī ayyuhā al-maliku al-saʿīdu anna malika al-Ṣīni qāla ītūnī bi-al-muzayyini wa-yakūnu sababa khalāṣikum wa-nadfinu hādhā al-aḥdaba fa-inna lahu min amsi mayyitun wa-naʿmalu lahu ḍarīḥan
sentences.l: She said: It has reached me, O king, the happy one, that the king of China said: Bring-me the barber — and he will be (the) cause of your deliverance — and we shall bury this hunchback, for to him from yesterday (he is) dead, and we shall make for him a tomb.
sentences.i: She said: It has reached me, O fortunate king, that the king of China said: "Bring me the barber; he will be the means of your deliverance. Then we shall bury this hunchback, who has been dead since yesterday, and build him a tomb."
sentences.n: The speaker is Shahrazād, resuming the story of the Hunchback. The print has ايتوني, which is read as إِيتُونِي, “bring me”, from أتى; the verb takes its object with بِـ, so “bring me the barber”. The king speaks in a run of imperative and “and”-clauses: the indicatives يكون and ندفن follow the command where Classical would use a jussive or subjunctive, and the print keeps them as they come. له من أمس ميت (“to him from yesterday, dead”) is the common way of saying “he has been dead since yesterday”.

sentences.t: فَمَا كَانَ إِلَّا سَاعَةٌ وَالْحَاجِبُ وَالْخَيَّاطُ مَضَوْا إِلَى الْحَبْسِ وَأَخْرَجُوا مِنْهُ الْمُزَيِّنَ وَسَارُوا بِهِ إِلَى أَنْ وَقَفُوا بَيْنَ يَدَيْ هَذَا الْمَلِكِ
sentences.tr: fa-mā kāna illā sāʿatun wa-al-ḥājibu wa-al-khayyāṭu maḍaw ilā al-ḥabsi wa-akhrajū minhu al-muzayyina wa-sārū bihi ilā an waqafū bayna yaday hādhā al-maliki
sentences.l: And it was not but an hour — and the chamberlain and the tailor (had) gone to the prison, and they brought-out from it the barber, and went with-him until they stood between the hands of this king.
sentences.i: It was no more than an hour before the chamberlain and the tailor had gone to the prison, brought the barber out of it, and led him along until they stood before the king.
sentences.n: فما كان إلا ساعة is a stock phrase for “it took no more than an hour”; the clause that follows, with its own subject, says what had happened by then. بين يدي (“between the hands of”) means “in the presence of”.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا رَآهُ وَتَأَمَّلَهُ فَإِذَا هُوَ شَيْخٌ كَبِيرٌ جَاوَزَ التِّسْعِينَ أَسْوَدُ الْوَجْهِ أَبْيَضُ اللِّحْيَةِ وَالْحَوَاجِبِ مُقَرْطَمُ الْآذَانِ طَوِيلُ الْأَنْفِ فِي نَفْسِهِ بَلْهَانُ فَضَحِكَ مِنْ رُؤْيَتِهِ الْمَلِكُ وَقَالَ لَهُ يَا صَامِتُ أُرِيدُ أَنْ يَحْكِيَ لِي شَيْأً مِنْ حِكَايَتِكَ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā raʾāhu wa-taʾammalahu fa-idhā huwa shaykhun kabīrun jāwaza al-tisʿīna aswadu al-wajhi abyaḍu al-liḥyati wa-al-ḥawājibi muqarṭamu al-ādhāni ṭawīlu al-anfi fī nafsihi balhānu fa-ḍaḥika min ruʾyatihi al-maliku wa-qāla lahu yā ṣāmitu urīdu an yaḥkiya lī shayʾan min ḥikāyatika
sentences.l: And when he saw him and looked him over, then behold, he (was) an old man, great (in years), who had passed the ninety; black of face, white of beard and eyebrows, clipped-of-ears, long of nose, in his self a simpleton. So laughed, at the sight of him, the king, and said to him: O Silent-one, I want that he tell me something of your story.
sentences.i: When the king saw him and looked him over, he beheld a very old man, past ninety, dark of face, white of beard and brows, with cropped ears and a long nose, and a simpleton at heart. The king laughed at the sight of him and said, "O Silent One, I want you to tell me something of your story."
sentences.n: فإذا هو … after فلما is the “and behold” that follows a first sight. مقرطم is rare and I take it as “clipped, cropped” (from قرطم, to cut off the tip); it may instead describe thick or oddly shaped ears, so the translation is a best guess. The print has يحكي (“that he tell”) where the sense wants “that you tell”: the king is speaking to the barber, so the third-person form is either a slip or a court-style indirectness, and it is vocalised as printed. The barber’s nickname الصامت, “the Silent”, is the joke of his story: he never stops talking.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ الْمُزَيِّنُ يَا مَلِكَ الزَّمَانِ وَمَا قِصَّةُ هَذَا النَّصْرَانِيِّ وَهَذَا الْيَهُودِيِّ وَهَذَا الْمُسْلِمِ وَهَذَا الْأَحْدَبِ الْمَيِّتِ بَيْنَكُمْ وَمَا سَبَبُ هَذَا الْجَمْعِ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla al-muzayyinu yā malika al-zamāni wa-mā qiṣṣatu hādhā al-naṣrāniyyi wa-hādhā al-yahūdiyyi wa-hādhā al-muslimi wa-hādhā al-aḥdabi al-mayyiti baynakum wa-mā sababu hādhā al-jamʿi
sentences.l: Then said the barber: O king of the age, and what (is) the story of this Christian, and this Jew, and this Muslim, and this hunchback, the dead one, among you, and what (is) the cause of this gathering?
sentences.i: Then the barber said, "O king of the age, what is the story of this Christian, this Jew, this Muslim, and this dead hunchback in your midst, and why are all these people gathered?"
sentences.n: The barber, who has been fetched from prison, knows nothing of the affair. The barber was not present for the tales told before he was fetched.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ لَهُ مَلِكُ الصِّينِ وَمَا سُؤَا لُكَ عَنْ هَذَا
sentences.tr: fa-qāla lahu maliku al-Ṣīni wa-mā suʾā luka ʿan hādhā
sentences.l: Then said to him the king of China: And what (is) your asking about this?
sentences.i: The king of China said to him, "And why do you ask about this?"
sentences.n: سوا لك is printed as two words but is سؤالك, “your question”; the print’s spacing is kept and the two halves are pointed so that they read as one word.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ سُؤَالِي عَنْهُمْ حَتَّى يَعْلَمَ الْمَلِكُ أَنِّي مَا أَنَا فُضُولِيٌّ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla suʾālī ʿanhum ḥattā yaʿlama al-maliku annī mā anā fuḍūliyyun
sentences.l: Then he said: My asking about them (is) so that the king may know that I, I am not a meddler,
sentences.i: He answered, "I ask about them so that the king may know that I am no busybody,
sentences.n: فضولي is a person who meddles in what does not concern him; the barber is protesting, with comic irony, that he is nothing of the kind.

sentences.t: وَأَنَا بَرِيءٌ مِمَّا اتَّهَمُونِي بِهِ مِنْ كَثْرَةِ الْكَلَامِ وَأَنَا الَّذِي اسْمِي الصَّامِتُ وَإِنَّ لِي نَصِيبًا مِنِ اسْمِي كَمَا قَالَ الشَّاءِ—رُ
sentences.tr: wa-anā barīʾun mimmā ittahamūnī bihi min kathrati al-kalāmi wa-anā alladhī ismī al-ṣāmitu wa-inna lī naṣīban min ismī ka-mā qāla al-shāʾ—ru
sentences.l: and I am innocent of what they accused me of — of much speech — and I (am) the one whose name (is) the Silent, and indeed to me (is) a share of my name, as said the poet:
sentences.i: and that I am innocent of what they charge me with, too much talk. I am the man named the Silent One, and I have my share of my name, as the poet says:
sentences.n: The print has الشاء—ر with a dash in the middle of the word; it is a misprint for الشاعر, “the poet”, and is kept as printed. اتهموني به … من كثرة الكلام is “they accused me of … namely of much talking”; the barber’s claim to be silent is the irony on which the whole tale turns.

sentences.t: وَقَلَّمَا اَبْصَرَتْ عَيْنَاكَ ذَالَقَبٍ * اِلَّا وَمَعْنَاهُ اِنْ فَتَّشْتَ فِي لَقَبِهِ
sentences.tr: wa-qallamā abṣarat ʿaynāka dhā-laqabin * illā wa-maʿnāhu in fattashta fī laqabihi
sentences.l: And seldom (have) seen your two eyes a-possessor-of a surname * but (that) its meaning, if you search, (is) in his surname.
sentences.i: Seldom do your eyes behold a man with a surname, * but, if you search it, you find its meaning in him.
sentences.n: Verse, copied as pointed in the print, which has ذالقب as one word (ذا لقب, “possessor of a surname”). The sense is that a nickname usually fits its bearer, which the barber applies to himself as الصامت.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ الْمَلِكُ اشْرَجُوا لِلْمُزَيِّنِ حَالَ هَذَا الْأَحْدَبِ وَمَا جَرَى لَهُ وَقْتَ الْعِشَاءِ وَمَا حَكَى النَّصْرَانِيُّ وَمَا حَكَى الْيَهُودِيُّ وَمَا حَكَى الشَّاهِلُ وَمَا حَكَى الْخَيَّاطُ وَلَيْسَ فِي الْإِعَادَةِ إِفَادَةٌ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla al-maliku ishrajū li-al-muzayyini ḥāla hādhā al-aḥdabi wa-mā jarā lahu waqta al-ʿishāʾi wa-mā ḥakā al-naṣrāniyyu wa-mā ḥakā al-yahūdiyyu wa-mā ḥakā al-shāhilu wa-mā ḥakā al-khayyāṭu wa-laysa fī al-iʿādati ifādatun
sentences.l: Then said the king: Explain to the barber the state of this hunchback and what happened to him at the time of supper, and what the Christian told, and what the Jew told, and what the witness told, and what the tailor told — and there is not, in the repeating, any benefit.
sentences.i: The king said, "Tell the barber how things stand with this hunchback, what befell him at suppertime, and what the Christian, the Jew, the witness and the tailor each related." And he added, "There is no profit in repeating it all."
sentences.n: The print has اشرجوا, which can only be a misprint for اشرحوا, “explain” (ج for ح); it is pointed as printed. الشاهل is likewise a slip for الشاهد, “the witness” (ل for د), as the same word is printed a few lines further on; it is vocalised as printed. The last clause is the king’s aside: the barber is to be told, but the tellers need not repeat their tales at length.

sentences.t: فَحَرَّكَ الْمُزَيِّنُ رَأْسَهُ وَقَالَ وَاللَّهِ إِنَّ هَذَا لَعَجِيبٌ عَجِيبٌ اكْشِفُوالِي عَنْ هَذَا لْأَحْدَبِ
sentences.tr: fa-ḥarraka al-muzayyinu raʾsahu wa-qāla wa-Allāhi inna hādhā la-ʿajībun ʿajībun ikshifūlī ʿan hādhā al-aḥdabi
sentences.l: Then the barber moved his head and said: By God, indeed this is surely strange, strange! Uncover for-me, from this, the hunchback.
sentences.i: The barber shook his head and said, "By God, this is strange indeed, passing strange! Uncover the hunchback for me."
sentences.n: اكشفوالي is printed as one word, اكشفوا لي, “uncover for me”, and لاحدب is الأحدب with its first alif dropped (هذا الأحدب); both are pointed as printed, the second with a bare lām. The doubled عجيب عجيب is an intensive, “very strange”.

sentences.t: فَكَشَفُوا لَهُ عَنْهُ فَجَلَسَ عِنْدَ رَأْسِهِ وَأَخَذَ رَأْسَهُ عَلَى حِجْرِهِ وَنَظَرَ فِي وَجْهِهِ وَضَحِكَ حَتَّى انْقَلَبَ عَلَى قَفَاهُ
sentences.tr: fa-kashafū lahu ʿanhu fa-jalasa ʿinda raʾsihi wa-akhadha raʾsahu ʿalā ḥijrihi wa-naẓara fī wajhihi wa-ḍaḥika ḥattā inqalaba ʿalā qafāhu
sentences.l: So they uncovered for him from him, and he sat at his head, and took his head on his lap, and looked in his face, and laughed until he turned over on his nape.
sentences.i: They uncovered the body for him, and he sat down by its head, took the head upon his lap, gazed into its face, and laughed until he fell over backward.
sentences.n: على قفاه, “on his nape”, is the idiom for falling on one’s back, as one does when helpless with laughter.

sentences.t: وَقَالَ لِكُلِّ مَوْتَةٍ عَجَبٌ وَمَوْتَةُ هَذَا الْأَحْدَبِ يَجِبُ أَنْ تُؤَرَّخَ بِمَاءِ الذَّهَبِ
sentences.tr: wa-qāla li-kulli mawtatin ʿajabun wa-mawtatu hādhā al-aḥdabi yajibu an tuʾarrakha bi-māʾi al-dhahabi
sentences.l: And he said: For every death (there is) a wonder, and the death of this hunchback it is necessary that it be dated/recorded with water of gold.
sentences.i: He said, "Every death has its marvel, but this hunchback’s death ought to be recorded in ink of gold."
sentences.n: تؤرخ (“be dated, be chronicled”) is the verb used again when the king orders the tale written down. ماء الذهب, “water of gold”, is gold ink, used for what is most worth preserving.

sentences.t: فَبَهِتَتِ الْجَمَاعَةُ مِنْ كَلَامِ الْمُزَيِّنِ وَتَعَجَّبَ الْمَلِكُ مِنْ كَلَامِهِ وَقَالَ مَالَكَ يَا صَامِتُ احْكِ لَنَا
sentences.tr: fa-bahitati al-jamāʿatu min kalāmi al-muzayyini wa-taʿajjaba al-maliku min kalāmihi wa-qāla mālaka yā ṣāmitu iḥki lanā
sentences.l: Then the company was struck-dumb at the barber’s speech, and the king marveled at his speech and said: What (ails) you, O Silent-one? Tell to us.
sentences.i: The company were struck dumb at the barber’s words, and the king marveled at them and said, "What is the matter, O Silent One? Tell us!"
sentences.n: مالك is printed joined (ما لك, “what is it with you?”). بهتت is the active form of بَهِتَ, “be dumbfounded”, where Classical more often has the passive بُهِتَتْ.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ الْمُزَيِّنُ يَا مَلِكَ الزَّمَانِ وَحَقِّ نِعْمَتِكَ الْأَحْدَبُ أَلَا كَذِبَ فِيهِ الرُّوحُ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla al-muzayyinu yā malika al-zamāni wa-ḥaqqi niʿmatika al-aḥdabu alā kadhiba fīhi al-rūḥu
sentences.l: Then said the barber: O king of the age, and by the right of your bounty, the hunchback — no lie! — in him (is) the spirit.
sentences.i: The barber said, "O king of the age, by the right of your bounty, this hunchback — no lie! — still has the breath of life in him."
sentences.n: وحق نعمتك is an oath, “by the right of your favour”. The print has الا كذب, which I read as أَلَا كَذِبَ, “no falsehood!”, a parenthesis like “no lie”; it could also be a stray إلا, and the reading is uncertain. The sense is clear either way: the hunchback is not dead.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ إِنَّ الْمُزَيِّنَ أَخْرَجَ مِنْ وَسَطِهِ حِرْمَدَانَ وَفَتَحَهُ وَأَخْرَجَ مِنْهُ مُكْحُلَةً فِيهَا دُهْنٌ وَدَهَنَ بِهِ رَقَبَةَ الْأَحْدَبِ وَعُرُوقَهَا
sentences.tr: thumma inna al-muzayyina akhraja min wasaṭihi ḥirmadānan wa-fataḥahu wa-akhraja minhu mukḥulatan fīhā duhnun wa-dahana bihi raqabata al-aḥdabi wa-ʿurūqahā
sentences.l: Then indeed the barber brought-out from his middle a case, and opened it, and brought-out from it a kohl-flask, in it oil, and anointed with-it the neck of the hunchback and its veins.
sentences.i: Then the barber drew from his waist a little case, opened it, and took out a flask in which there was an ointment, and with it he anointed the hunchback’s neck and its veins.
sentences.n: حرمدان is a rare word; I take it to be the barber’s kit-case, and the spelling may reflect a Persian-derived original. المكحلة is properly a kohl-flask, here holding salve.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ أَخْرَجَ كَلْبَتَيْنِ مِنْ حَدِيدٍ وَنَزَلَ بِهِمَا فِي حَلْقِهِ فَطَلَعَ قِطْعَةُ السَّمَكِ بِعَظْمِهَا
sentences.tr: thumma akhraja kalbatayni min ḥadīdin wa-nazala bihimā fī ḥalqihi fa-ṭalaʿa qiṭʿatu al-samaki bi-ʿaẓmihā
sentences.l: Then he brought-out two tongs of iron, and went-down with-them into his throat, and came-up the piece of the fish with its bone.
sentences.i: Then he took out a pair of iron tongs, lowered them down the hunchback’s throat, and up came the piece of fish with its bone.
sentences.n: طلع precedes its feminine subject قطعة without agreeing with it, a normal feature of this sort of Arabic when the verb comes first. The tailor’s tale told how the hunchback choked on a fish-bone at supper.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا طَلَعَ بِهَا وَإِذَا هِيَ مَغْمُوسَةٌ دَمًا وَالْأَحْدَبُ عَطَسَ عَطْسَةً ثُمَّ نَطَّ وَوَقَفَ عَلَى حَيْلِهِ وَمَلَّسَ عَلَى وَجْهِهِ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā ṭalaʿa bihā wa-idhā hiya maghmūsatun daman wa-al-aḥdabu ʿaṭasa ʿaṭsatan thumma naṭṭa wa-waqafa ʿalā ḥaylihi wa-mallasa ʿalā wajhihi
sentences.l: And when it came-up with-it — and behold, it (was) dipped (in) blood — and the hunchback sneezed a sneeze, then leapt and stood on his strength, and stroked over his face.
sentences.i: And as it came up, soaked in blood, the hunchback sneezed a great sneeze, then leapt to his feet and passed his hand over his face.
sentences.n: The sentence is not finished grammatically: فلما … has no main clause, and the print runs on with وإذا, “and behold”, a feature of loose Middle Arabic narrative. طلع بها is read as “it came up with it”, that is, the fish-bone came out held in the tongs. على حيله, “on his strength”, I take to mean “on his own legs”.

sentences.t: وَقَالَ أَشْهَدُ أَنْ لَا إِلَٰهَ إِلَّا اللَّهُ وَأَشْهَدُ أَنَّ مُحَمَّدًا رَسُولُ اللَّهِ
sentences.tr: wa-qāla ashhadu an lā ilāha illā Allāhu wa-ashhadu anna Muḥammadan rasūlu Allāhi
sentences.l: And he said: I bear-witness that (there is) no god but God, and I bear-witness that Muḥammad (is) the messenger of God.
sentences.i: Then he said, "I bear witness that there is no god but God, and I bear witness that Muḥammad is the Messenger of God."
sentences.n: The profession of faith. اله is printed without its alif and is pointed with the dagger alif.

sentences.t: فَتَعَجَّبَ الْمَلِكُ وَالْحَاضِرُونَ مِنَ الَّذِي رَأَوْهُ وَ عَايَنُوهُ
sentences.tr: fa-taʿajjaba al-maliku wa-al-ḥāḍirūna mina alladhī raʾawhu wa- ʿāyanūhu
sentences.l: Then marveled the king and those-present at that which they saw and witnessed.
sentences.i: The king and all who were present marveled at what they had seen with their own eyes.
sentences.n: The print breaks the line after a lone و, so وعاينوه is two words in the archive; the spacing is kept.

sentences.t: فَضَحِكَ مَلِكُ الصِّينِ حَتَّى غُشِيَ عَلَيْهِ وَكَذَٰلِكَ الْحَاضِرُونَ
sentences.tr: fa-ḍaḥika maliku al-Ṣīni ḥattā ghushiya ʿalayhi wa-ka-dhālika al-ḥāḍirūna
sentences.l: Then laughed the king of China until it was covered over him — and in-that-way those-present.
sentences.i: The king of China laughed until he swooned, and so did all who were present.
sentences.n: غُشي عليه (“it was covered over him”) is the usual way to say that someone fainted. Here it is laughter that overcomes him.

sentences.t: وَقَالَ السُّلْطَانُ وَاللَّهِ إِنَّ هَذِهِ قِصَّةٌ عَجِيبَةٌ مَا رَأَيْتُ أَعْرَبَ مِنْهَا
sentences.tr: wa-qāla al-sulṭānu wa-Allāhi inna hādhihi qiṣṣatun ʿajībatun mā raʾaytu aʿraba minhā
sentences.l: And said the sultan: By God, indeed this (is) a story, strange; I have not seen (one) more [aʿrab] than it.
sentences.i: The sultan said, "By God, this is a strange tale; I have never seen a stranger."
sentences.n: The print has اعرب, which I vocalise as printed; the sense required is “stranger”, so it is most likely a misprint or variant of أغرب (ع for غ). The “sultan” is the king of China, named by both titles.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ إِنَّ السُّلْطَانَ قَالَ يَا مُسْلِمِينَ يَا جَمَاعَةُ أَعَسْكَرُ عُمْرَكُمْ رَأَيْتُمْ أَحَدًا يَمُوتُ ثُمَّ يَحْيَى
sentences.tr: thumma inna al-sulṭāna qāla yā muslimīna yā jamāʿatu aʿaskaru ʿumrakum raʾaytum aḥadan yamūtu thumma yaḥyā
sentences.l: Then indeed the sultan said: O Muslims, O company, O troop — your life-long you have seen someone die and then live?
sentences.i: Then the sultan said, "O Muslims, O company, O soldiers, have you ever in your lives seen a man die and then come back to life?"
sentences.n: اعسكر is read as أَعَسْكَرُ, “O soldiery”, with the vocative particle أ, as the third in a series of appeals after يا مسلمين and يا جماعة; the reading is a guess. عمركم is the accusative of time, “in your lifetime”, and the yes-or-no question has no particle, only the tone.

sentences.t: وَلَوْلَا رَزَقَهُ اللَّهُ بِهَذَا الْمُزَيِّنِ فَإِنَّهُ كَانَ سَبَبًا لِحَيَاةِ لَكَٰنَ يَمُوتُ
sentences.tr: wa-lawlā razaqahu Allāhu bi-hādhā al-muzayyini fa-innahu kāna sababan li-ḥayāti lakāna yamūtu
sentences.l: And had not God provided him with this barber — for he was a cause for (the) life (of him) — he would (have) died.
sentences.i: Had God not provided him with this barber, who was the cause of his life, he would have died.
sentences.n: Three things in the print are irregular. لولا is followed by a verb (رزقه الله) instead of a noun; حياة seems to lack its pronoun, “his life”; and لكن, normally “but”, is read here as لكان, “he would have”, with the dagger alif for the missing alif, since only that reading completes the “had not … he would have” construction.

sentences.t: فَقَالُوا وَاللَّهِ إِنَّ هَذَا عَجَبٌ عَجِيبٌ
sentences.tr: fa-qālū wa-Allāhi inna hādhā ʿajabun ʿajībun
sentences.l: Then they said: By God, indeed this (is) a wonder, wondrous.
sentences.i: They said, "By God, this is a wonder indeed!"
sentences.n: عجب عجيب, “a wonder, wondrous”, is the same intensifying pairing the barber used earlier.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ إِنَّ مَلِكَ الصِّينِ أَمَرَأَنْ تُؤَرَّخَ هَذِهِ الْقِصَّةُ فَأَرَّخُوهَا ثُمَّ جَعَلُوهَا فِي خِزَانَةِ الْمَلِكِ
sentences.tr: thumma inna malika al-Ṣīni amara an tuʾarrakha hādhihi al-qiṣṣatu fa-arrakhūhā thumma jaʿalūhā fī khizānati al-maliki
sentences.l: Then indeed the king of China commanded that be recorded this story, and they recorded it, then put it in the treasury of the king.
sentences.i: Then the king of China ordered that this story be written down, and they wrote it down and placed it in the royal treasury.
sentences.n: امران is printed as one word, أمر أن, “he ordered that”; the print’s spacing is kept. ان after أمر takes the passive subjunctive تؤرخ with a feminine subject, “this story”. خزانة is a repository, so here the royal archive as well as the treasury.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ خَلَعَ عَلَى الْيَهُودِيِّ وَالنَّصْرَانِيِّ وَالشَّاهِدِ كُلَّ وَاحِدٍ خِلْعَةً سَنِيَّةً وَأَمَرَهُمْ بِالِانْصِرَافِ فَانْصَرَفُوا
sentences.tr: thumma khalaʿa ʿalā al-yahūdiyyi wa-al-naṣrāniyyi wa-al-shāhidi kulla wāḥidin khilʿatan saniyyatan wa-amarahum bi-al-inṣirāfi fa-inṣarafū
sentences.l: Then he bestowed-a-robe upon the Jew and the Christian and the witness, each one a robe, lofty, and commanded them to the departing, and they departed.
sentences.i: Then he bestowed a splendid robe of honor on each of them, the Jew, the Christian and the witness, and bade them depart, and they departed.
sentences.n: خلع على (“to cast a robe upon”) is the regular verb for presenting a robe of honor, which is the king’s mark of favor throughout the tale. The nouns after it are in apposition: “each one, a splendid robe”.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ أَقْبَلَ السُّلْطَانُ عَلَى الْخَيَّاطِ وَخَلَعَ عَلَيْهِ خِلْعَةً سَنِيَّةً وَجَعَلَهُ خَيَّاطَهُ وَرَتَّبَ لَهُ الرَّوَاتِبَ وَأَصْلَحَ بَيْنَهُ وَبَيْنَ الْأَحْدَبِ
sentences.tr: thumma aqbala al-sulṭānu ʿalā al-khayyāṭi wa-khalaʿa ʿalayhi khilʿatan saniyyatan wa-jaʿalahu khayyāṭahu wa-rattaba lahu al-rawātiba wa-aṣlaḥa baynahu wa-bayna al-aḥdabi
sentences.l: Then the sultan turned toward the tailor, and bestowed-a-robe upon him, a robe, lofty, and made him his tailor, and appointed for him the allowances, and set-right between him and the hunchback.
sentences.i: Then the sultan turned to the tailor, gave him a splendid robe, made him his own tailor, assigned him a regular allowance, and reconciled him with the hunchback.
sentences.n: The tailor’s allowances (الرواتب) are fixed stipends. أصلح بينه وبين الأحدب is the idiom for making peace between two parties.

sentences.t: وَخَلَعَ عَلَى الْأَحْدَبِ خِلْعَةً سَنِيَّةً مَلِيحَةً وَرَتَّبَ لَهُ الرَّوَاتِبَ وَجَعَلَهُ نَدِيمَهُ
sentences.tr: wa-khalaʿa ʿalā al-aḥdabi khilʿatan saniyyatan malīḥatan wa-rattaba lahu al-rawātiba wa-jaʿalahu nadīmahu
sentences.l: And he bestowed-a-robe upon the hunchback, a robe, lofty, handsome, and appointed for him the allowances, and made him his boon-companion.
sentences.i: He gave the hunchback a splendid and handsome robe too, assigned him an allowance, and made him his boon companion.
sentences.n: النديم is the king’s companion at the wine-cup and the conversation, a court post.

sentences.t: وَأَنْعَمَ عَلَى الْمُزَيِّنِ وَخَلَعَ عَلَيْهِ خِلْعَةً وَجَعَلَ لَهُ جَامَكِيَّةً وَجَعَلَهُ مُزَيِّنَ الْمَمْلَكَةِ وَنَدِيمَهُ
sentences.tr: wa-anʿama ʿalā al-muzayyini wa-khalaʿa ʿalayhi khilʿatan wa-jaʿala lahu jāmakiyyatan wa-jaʿalahu muzayyina al-mamlakati wa-nadīmahu
sentences.l: And he showed-favor to the barber and bestowed-a-robe upon him, a robe, and made for him a stipend, and made him barber of the kingdom and his boon-companion.
sentences.i: He showered favors on the barber, gave him a robe, set a salary on him, and made him barber of the realm and his own boon companion.
sentences.n: جامكية is the stipend paid to a court servant; the word is of Persian origin.

sentences.t: وَلَمْ يَزَٰلُوا فِى أَلَذِّ عَيْشٍ وَأَهْنَاهُ إِى أَنْ أَتَاهُمْ هَادِمُ اللَّذَّاتِ وَمُفَرِّقُ الْجَمَاعَاتِ
sentences.tr: wa-lam yazālū fī aladhdhi ʿayshin wa-ahnāhu ilā an atāhum hādimu al-ladhdhāti wa-mufarriqu al-jamāʿāti
sentences.l: And they did-not cease in the sweetest of life and the most pleasant of it, until came to them the demolisher of pleasures and the parter of gatherings.
sentences.i: They went on in the sweetest and happiest of lives until there came to them the one who ends every pleasure and scatters every gathering.
sentences.n: The print has يزلوا without the long ā of يزالوا (vocalised with the dagger alif) and اى for إلى, “until”, with the lām dropped, both kept as printed. The last two phrases are the stock names for death, which closes a tale in the Nights.

sentences.t: وَلَيْسَ هَذَا بِأَعْجَبَ مِنْ قِصَّةِ الْوَزِيرَيْنِ وَأَنِيسِ الْجَلِيسِ
sentences.tr: wa-laysa hādhā bi-aʿjaba min qiṣṣati al-wazīrayni wa-anīsi al-jalīsi
sentences.l: And this is not more wondrous than the story of the two viziers and Anīs al-Jalīs.
sentences.i: But this is no stranger than the tale of the two viziers and Anīs al-Jalīs.
sentences.n: Shahrazād’s hook for the next tale. The bi- on أعجب is the pleonastic one that follows ليس, and it governs a comparative, which is why the ending is a fatḥa.

sentences.t: قَالَتْ لَهَا وَكَيْفَ ذَٰلِكَ قَالَتْ
sentences.tr: qālat lahā wa-kayfa dhālika qālat
sentences.l: She said to her: And how (is) that? She said:
sentences.i: Her sister said to her, "And how is that?" She said:
sentences.n: Dunyāzād, Shahrazād’s sister, asks the question that brings on the next tale; the next night’s text continues Shahrazād’s answer.

sentences.t: بَلَغَنِي أَيُّهَا الْمَلِكُ السَّعِيدُ أَنَّهُ كَانَ بِالْبَصْرَةِ مَلِكٌ مِنَ الْمُلُوكِ يُحِبُّ الْفُقَرَاءَ وَالصَّعَالِيكَ وَيُحِبُّ الرَّعِيَّةَ وَيَهَبُ مِنْ مَالِهِ لِمَنْ يُؤْمِنُ بِمُحَمَّدٍ صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ
sentences.tr: balaghanī ayyuhā al-maliku al-saʿīdu annahu kāna bi-al-baṣrati malikun mina al-mulūki yuḥibbu al-fuqarāʾa wa-al-ṣaʿālīka wa-yuḥibbu al-raʿiyyata wa-yahabu min mālihi li-man yuʾminu bi-Muḥammadin ṣallā Allāhu ʿalayhi wa-sallama
sentences.l: It has reached me, O king, the happy one, that there was in Basra a king of the kings, loving the poor-ones and the vagabonds, and loving the flock (the subjects), and giving from his wealth to whoever believes in Muḥammad — God bless him and give him peace.
sentences.i: It has reached me, O fortunate king, that there was in Basra a king among kings who loved the poor and the wandering beggars and cherished his subjects, and who gave of his wealth to whoever believed in Muḥammad, God bless him and grant him peace.
sentences.n: This is the opening formula of the night. الصعاليك (ṣaʿālīk) are penniless vagabonds. Note that the king’s generosity is aimed at Muslims; the story that follows is set in a Muslim Basra under a king of the Zaynī line.

sentences.t: وَهُوَ كَمَا قَالَ فِيهِ بَعْضُ وَاصِفِيهِ شِعْرٌ
sentences.tr: wa-huwa ka-mā qāla fīhi baʿḍu wāṣifīhi shiʿrun
sentences.l: and he is as said of him some of his describers — verse:
sentences.i: and he was just as one of those who described him said in verse:

sentences.t:
مَلِكٌ اِذَا جَالَتْ عَلَيْهِ مَوَاكِبٌ * اَرَبَ الْعِدَاةَ بِكُلِّ عَضْبٍ اَنْتَرِى
وَيَخُطُّ خَطًّا فِى الصُّدُورِ اِذَا سَطَا * يَوْمًا تَرَاهُ عَلَى الْفَوَارِسِ مُفْتَرِي
sentences.tr:
malikun idhā jālat ʿalayhi mawākibun * araba al-ʿidāta bi-kulli ʿaḍbin antarī
wa-yakhuṭṭu khaṭṭan fī al-ṣudūri idhā saṭā * yawman tarāhu ʿalā al-fawārisi muftarī
sentences.l:
A king, when troops of riders wheel about him, * he cuts-off (the limbs of) the enemies with every keen blade, antarī,
and he draws a line in the breasts when he assaults * on a day you see him upon the horsemen, one-who-rends.
sentences.i:
A king: when squadrons wheel around him, * he hews down the enemy with every keen blade, antarī,
and he draws a line across their breasts when he strikes, * a day on which you see him among the horsemen, rending them.
sentences.n: Verse, copied as pointed in the print. Two words are doubtful. اَرَبَ is read as arraba/araba, “to cut off (a limb at the joint)” (Lane), which suits the context; and اَنْتَرِى at the end of the first line is obscure and may be corrupt — it is left as printed and not translated. مُفْتَرِي is taken as “one who rends”, from فرى, rather than “inventor, liar”. The line leaves the metre uncertain.

sentences.t: وَكَانَ يُقَالُ لَهُ الْمَلِكُ مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ سُلَيْمَانَ الزَّيْنِيُّ وَكَانَ لَهُ وَزِيرَيْنِ أَحَدُهُمَا يُقَالُ لَهُ الْمُعِينُ بْنُ سَاوِى وَالثَّانِي يُقَالُ لَهُ الْفَضْلُ بْنُ خَاقَانَ
sentences.tr: wa-kāna yuqālu lahu al-maliku Muḥammadu ibnu Sulaymāna al-Zaynīyyu wa-kāna lahu wazīrayni aḥaduhumā yuqālu lahu al-Muʿīnu ibnu Sāwī wa-al-thānī yuqālu lahu al-Faḍlu ibnu Khāqāna
sentences.l: And it used to be said to him, the king Muḥammad son-of Sulayman al-Zayni, and there was to him two viziers, one-of-them it is said to him al-Muʿīn son-of Sāwī and the second it is said to him al-Faḍl son-of Khāqān.
sentences.i: He was called King Muḥammad ibn Sulayman al-Zayni, and he had two viziers: one was called al-Muʿīn ibn Sāwī, and the second was called al-Faḍl ibn Khāqān.
sentences.n: وزيرين is printed in the accusative/oblique dual where Classical Arabic wants the nominative وزيران as the subject of كان لـ; vocalised as printed. This is a common Middle Arabic habit of treating the dual as invariable. The first vizier’s father’s name is spelt ساوى here and ساوي below; both are one name.

sentences.t: وَكَانَ الْفَضْلُ بْنُ خَاقَانَ أَكْرَمَ أَهْلِ زَمَانِهِ حَسَنَ السِّيرَةِ أَجْمَعَتِ الْقُلُوبُ عَلَى مَحَبَّتِهِ وَأَجْمَعَتِ النَّاسُ عَلَى مَشُورَتِهِ وَالْكُلُّ يَدْعُونَ لَهُ بِطُولِ مُدَّتِهِ لِأَنَّهُ مَحْضُ خَيْرٍ مُزِيلُ الشَّرِّ وَالضَّيْرِ
sentences.tr: wa-kāna al-Faḍlu ibnu Khāqāna akrama ahli zamānihi ḥasana al-sīrati ajmaʿati al-qulūbu ʿalā maḥabbatihi wa-ajmaʿati al-nāsu ʿalā mashūratihi wa-al-kullu yadʿūna lahu bi-ṭūli muddatihi li-annahu maḥḍu khayrin muzīlu al-sharri wa-al-ḍayri
sentences.l: And al-Faḍl son-of Khāqān was the most generous of the people of his time, good-of the conduct: the hearts agreed upon love of him, and the people agreed upon his counsel, and all of them pray for him with length of his term, because he was pure good, remover-of the evil and the harm.
sentences.i: Al-Fadl ibn Khāqān was the most generous man of his age and of excellent conduct: all hearts were united in loving him and all people were agreed on seeking his counsel, and everyone prayed for him to have a long life, for he was pure goodness, a remover of evil and harm.
sentences.n: The second أجمعت has a feminine verb with the masculine-sense plural الناس as subject, and الكل يدعون has a plural verb after a singular “all”: both agree with the sense rather than the form, common in Middle Arabic. The clause “the hearts agreed … and the people agreed” falls into a rhymed pair (محبته / مشورته).

sentences.t: وَكَانَ الْوَزِيرُ الْمُعِينُ بْنُ سَاوِي يَكْرَهُ النَّاسَ وَلَا يُحِبُّ الْخَيْرَ وَكَانَ مَحْضَ سُوءٍ كَمَا قِيلَ فِيهِ شِعْ
sentences.tr: wa-kāna al-wazīru al-Muʿīnu ibnu Sāwī yakrahu al-nāsa wa-lā yuḥibbu al-khayra wa-kāna maḥḍa sūʾin ka-mā qīla fīhi shiʿ
sentences.l: And the vizier al-Muʿīn son-of Sāwī used to hate the people and not love the good, and he was pure evil, as was said of him — verse:
sentences.i: The vizier al-Muʿīn ibn Sāwī hated people and had no love of goodness; he was pure evil, as the poet said of him:
sentences.n: The word شعر (verse) is printed cut short as شع, and is vocalised as printed; the line then ends with a dash, introducing the verse.

sentences.t:
لُذْ بِالْكِرَامِ بَنِي الْكِرَامِ فَإِنَّمَا * تَلِدُ الْكِرَامُ بَنُوا الْكِرَامِ كِرَامًا
وَدَعِ اللِّئَامَ بَنِي اللِّئَامِ فَإِنَّمَا * تَلِدُ اللِّئَامُ بَنُوا اللِّئَامِ لِئَامًا
sentences.tr:
ludh bi-al-kirāmi banī al-kirāmi fa-innamā * talidu al-kirāmu banū al-kirāmi kirāman
wa-daʿi al-liʾāma banī al-liʾāmi fa-innamā * talidu al-liʾāmu banū al-liʾāmi liʾāman
sentences.l:
Take-refuge with the noble-ones, sons of the noble-ones, for indeed * the noble-ones beget — sons of the noble-ones — noble-ones,
and leave the base-ones, sons of the base-ones, for indeed * the base-ones beget — sons of the base-ones — base-ones.
sentences.i:
Seek shelter with the noble, the sons of the noble, for * it is the noble who beget — sons of the noble — noble children;
and leave the base, the sons of the base, for * it is the base who beget — sons of the base — base children.
sentences.n: The verse plays on repeated roots: the noble (kirām) beget the noble, and the base (liʾām) beget the base, each line pairing the stock with its offspring.

sentences.t: قَالَ وَكَانَ النَّاسُ عَلَى قَدْرِ مَحَبَّتِهِمْ لِلْفَضْلِ بْنِ خَاقَانَ عَلَى قَدْرِ بُغْضِهِمْ لِلْمُعِينِ بْنِ سَاوِي
sentences.tr: qāla wa-kāna al-nāsu ʿalā qadri maḥabbatihim li-al-Faḍli ibni Khāqāna ʿalā qadri bughḍihim li-al-Muʿīni ibni Sāwī
sentences.l: He said: and the people were, according to the measure of their love for al-Faḍl son-of Khāqān, according to the measure of their hatred for al-Muʿīn son-of Sāwī.
sentences.i: He said: and people’s hatred of al-Muʿīn ibn Sāwī was as great as their love for al-Faḍl ibn Khāqān.
sentences.n: The speaker is still Shahrazād; “he said” is the narrator’s routine reminder that the story is being retold.

sentences.t: وَبِقُدْرَةِ الْقَادِرِ أَنَّ الْمَلِكَ مُحَمَّدَ بْنَ سُلَيْمَانَ الزَّيْنِيَّ يَوْمًا مِنَ الْأَيَّامِ قَاعِدٌ عَلَى كُرْسِيِّ مَمْلَكَتِهِ وَحَوْلَهُ أَرْبَابُ دَوْلَتِهِ إِذْنَادَى وَزِيرَهُ الْفَضْلَ بْنَ خَاقَانَ
sentences.tr: wa-bi-qudrati al-qādiri anna al-malika Muḥammada ibna Sulaymāna al-Zaynīya yawman mina al-ayyāmi qāʿidun ʿalā kursiyyi mamlakatihi wa-ḥawlahu arbābu dawlatihi idhnādā wazīrahu al-Faḍla ibna Khāqāna
sentences.l: And by the power of the Powerful-one, that the king Muḥammad son-of Sulayman al-Zayni, one day of the days, sitting upon the throne of his kingdom, and around him the lords of his state — (when) he called his vizier al-Faḍl son-of Khāqān
sentences.i: And by the power of the Almighty, it happened one day that King Muḥammad ibn Sulayman al-Zayni was sitting on the throne of his kingdom with the lords of his state about him, when he called his vizier al-Faḍl ibn Khāqān
sentences.n: The sentence begins with a formula, وبقدرة القادر, “by the power of the Almighty”, which marks a turn of fate. Then أن takes قاعد in the nominative, a Middle Arabic slip that is vocalised as printed (Classical Arabic wants قاعدًا). اذنادى is printed as one word; it is read as إذ نادى, “when he called”, but kept joined as in the print.

sentences.t: وَقَالَ لَهُ الْمَلِكُ أُرِيدُ جَارِيَةً لَا يَكُونُ فِي زَمَنِهَا أَحْسَنُ مِنْهَا تَكُونُ كَامِلَةً فِي الْجَمَالِ فَائِقَةً فِي الاِعْتِدَالِ حَمِيدَةَ الْخِصَالِ
sentences.tr: wa-qāla lahu al-maliku urīdu jāriyatan lā yakūnu fī zamanihā aḥsanu minhā takūnu kāmilatan fī al-jamāli fāʾiqatan fī al-iʿtidāli ḥamīdata al-khiṣāli
sentences.l: and he said to him, the king: I want a girl, there will not be in her time (one) more beautiful than her; she should be perfect in beauty, surpassing in (bodily) balance, praiseworthy-of the qualities.
sentences.i: and said to him, “I want a slave-girl such that none in her day will be lovelier: perfect in beauty, surpassing in proportion, and praiseworthy in her qualities.”
sentences.n: The king’s speech has no “saying” particle after قال له; it begins at أريد. Here الملك after “he said to him” is the subject (“the king said”). جارية means a young female slave, here a concubine to be bought. The three descriptive phrases are rhymed in -āl.

sentences.t: فَقَالَتْ أَرْبَابُ الدَّوْلَةِ هَذِهِ لَاتُوجَدُ إِلَّا بِعَشَرَةِ آلَافِ دِينَارٍ
sentences.tr: fa-qālat arbābu al-dawlati hādhihi lātūjadu illā bi-ʿasharati ālāfi dīnārin
sentences.l: So said the lords of the state: This one is not found except with ten thousand dinars.
sentences.i: The lords of the state said, “A girl like that cannot be found for less than ten thousand dinars.”
sentences.n: فقالت is a feminine verb before the plural ارباب, normal for a plural of things or persons in Classical Arabic; لاتوجد is printed as one word. The بِـ after إلا is the “price” بِـ: “for, at the cost of”.

sentences.t: فَعِنْدَ ذَلِكَ زَعَقَ السُّلْطَانُ عَلَى خَازِنْدَارٍ وَقَالَ احْمِلْ عَشَرَةَ آلَافِ دِينَارٍ إِلَى دَارَالْفَضْلِ بْنِ خَاقَانَ فَامْتَثَلَ الْخَازِنْدَارُ أَمْرَالسُّلْطَانِ
sentences.tr: fa-ʿinda dhālika zaʿaqa al-sulṭānu ʿalā khāzindārin wa-qāla iḥmil ʿasharata ālāfi dīnārin ilā dāra al-Faḍli ibni Khāqāna fa-imtathala al-khāzindāru amra al-sulṭāni
sentences.l: So at that, the sultan shouted at a treasurer and said: Carry ten thousand dinars to the house of al-Faḍl son-of Khāqān; and the treasurer complied with the command of the sultan.
sentences.i: At that the sultan called out to his treasurer and said, “Carry ten thousand dinars to the house of al-Faḍl ibn Khāqān.” The treasurer obeyed the sultan’s command.
sentences.n: خازندار (khāzindār) is a Persian-derived title, “treasurer”; زعق is a colloquial “to cry out, shout”. دارالفضل and امرالسلطان are printed with the first noun run into the second, and are kept joined; read dār al-Faḍl and amr al-sulṭān.

sentences.t: وَ نَزَلَ الْوَزِيرُ بَعْدَ مَارَسَمَ لَهُ السُّلْطَانُ أَنْ يَعْمِدَاِلَى السُّوقِ كُلَّ يَوْمٍ وَيُوصِىَ السَّمَاسِرَةَ عَلَى مَا ذَكَرْنَاهُ وَأَنْ لَاتُبَاعَ جَارِيَةٌ ثَمَنُهَا فَوْقَ الْأَلْفِ دِينَارٍ حَتَّى تُعْرَضَ عَلَى الْوَزِيرِ
sentences.tr: wa-nazala al-wazīru baʿda mā rasama lahu al-sulṭānu an yaʿmida ilā al-sūqi kulla yawmin wa-yūṣiya al-samāsirata ʿalā mā dhakarnāhu wa-an lā tubāʿa jāriyatun thamanuhā fawqa al-alfi dīnārin ḥattā tuʿraḍa ʿalā al-wazīri
sentences.l: And the vizier went down, after what the sultan had decreed to him: that he betake himself to the market every day and charge the brokers with what we have mentioned, and that no girl be sold whose price is above the thousand dinars until she is shown to the vizier.
sentences.i: Then the vizier went down, as the sultan had ordered him, to go to the market every day and instruct the brokers as we have said: that no slave-girl priced above a thousand dinars was to be sold until she had been shown to the vizier.
sentences.n: The line-break leaves a stray و before نزل; it is kept as printed (و نزل), and read as an ordinary “and”. مارسم is printed as one word. يعمدالى is printed as one word (read yaʿmida ilā). السماسرة (samāsira) are the market brokers.

sentences.t: فَلَمْ تَبِعِ السَّمَاسِرَةُ جَارِيَةً حَتَّى يَعْرِضُونَهَا وَكُلُّ جَارِيَةٍ وَقَعَتْ لَهُمْ لَمْ يُعْجِبْهَا الْوَزِيرُ
sentences.tr: fa-lam tabiʿi al-samāsiratu jāriyatan ḥattā yaʿriḍūnahā wa-kullu jāriyatin waqaʿat lahum lam yuʿjibhā al-wazīru
sentences.l: So the brokers did not sell a girl until they would show her, and every girl that fell to them, the vizier was not pleased with her.
sentences.i: So the brokers sold no girl until they had shown her to him, and the vizier liked none of the girls that came to them.
sentences.n: يعرضونها has the indicative ending -ūna after حتى, where Classical Arabic wants the subjunctive (yaʿriḍūhā); it is vocalised as printed. The last clause is a topic (“every girl … the vizier did not like her”), with the pronoun resumed in يعجبها.

sentences.t: فَنِي يَوْمٍ مِنَ الْأَيَّامِ وَإِذَا بِالسِّمْسَارِ أَقْبَلَ إِلَى دَارَالْوَزِيرِ الْفَضْلِ بْنِ خَاقَانَ فَوَجَدَهُ رَاكِبًا طَالِبَ الْمَسِيرِ لِقَصْرِ الْمَلِكِ فَدَقَّ فِي رِكَا بِ وَأَنْشَدَ يَقُولُ
sentences.tr: fa-nī yawmin mina al-ayyāmi wa-idhā bi-al-simsāri aqbala ilā dāra al-wazīri al-Faḍli ibni Khāqāna fa-wajadahu rākiban ṭāliba al-masīri li-qaṣri al-maliki fa-daqqa fī rikā bi wa-anshada yaqūlu
sentences.l: So in a day of the days, and behold, with the broker: he came to the house of the vizier al-Faḍl son-of Khāqān, and found him mounted, seeking the going to the palace of the king, and he knocked at (his) stirrup, and recited, saying:
sentences.i: One day, behold, a broker came to the house of the vizier al-Faḍl ibn Khāqān and found him mounted and about to ride to the king’s palace. He tapped at the vizier’s stirrup and recited:
sentences.n: The print has فني, evidently for في (“in a day of the days”) with a stray ن; it is vocalised as it stands and read fī. The بِـ after وإذا only marks what appears: “and behold, a broker”. ركا ب is printed split with a dash after it, and is read rikāb, “stirrup”, perhaps for ركابه, “his stirrup”, cut off by the printer. فدق في is “knocked at” or “struck at”.

sentences.t:
يَا مَنْ اعَادَ سُومَ الْمُلْكِ مَنْشُوراً * اَنْتَ الْوَزِيرُ الَّذِي لَازِلْتَ مَسْرُورًا
اَحْيَيْتَ مَا مَاتَ بَيْنَ النَّاسِ مِنْ كَرَمٍ * لَا زَالَ سَعْيُكَ عِنْدَ اللَّهِ مَشْكُورًا
sentences.tr:
yā man aʿāda sūma al-mulki manshūran * anta al-wazīru alladhī lāzilta masrūran
aḥyayta mā māta bayna al-nāsi min karamin * lā zāla saʿyuka ʿinda Allāhi mashkūran
sentences.l:
O you who brought-back the sūm of kingship spread-out, * you are the vizier who have never ceased (to be) delighted,
you revived what died among the people of generosity; * may your striving never cease to be thanked before God.
sentences.i:
O you who made the glory of kingship unfurl again, * you are the vizier who has never ceased to be glad;
you revived the generosity that had died among men: * may your efforts be thanked before God forever.
sentences.n: Verse, copied as pointed in the print. سُوم is obscure here; it is left as printed, and may be a corruption of رسم, “the established way”, or taken as “the market-price, the worth” of kingship. منشورا is “spread out, unfurled”, as of a banner. The shift between “you” and “who” (انت الوزير الذي لازلت) is a Middle Arabic liberty, kept as printed.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ قَٰلَ يَا سَيِّدِي أَنَّ الَّذِي سَبَقَ بِهِ الْمَرْسُومُ الْكَرِيمُ بِطَلَبِهِ قَدْ حَضَرَ
sentences.tr: thumma qāla yā sayyidī anna alladhī sabaqa bihi al-marsūmu al-karīmu bi-ṭalabihi qad ḥaḍara
sentences.l: Then he said: O my lord, that the one with whom the noble decree went before, in the asking-for-him, has arrived.
sentences.i: Then he said, "My lord, the one for whom the noble decree was sent out has arrived."
sentences.n: The print writes قل for قال; it is read with the dagger alif. The speaker is the broker, as the lines below show (the vizier turns to the السمسار). سبق به المرسوم, 'the decree went ahead concerning him', means the order to summon him had already been given.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ لَهُ الْوَزِيرُ عَلَيَّ بِهَا
sentences.tr: fa-qāla lahu al-wazīru ʿalayya bihā
sentences.l: So the vizier said to him: Upon me, with her!
sentences.i: Then the vizier said to him, "Bring her to me!"
sentences.n: عليّ بـ is a set command, 'bring (so-and-so) to me': the بِـ marks what is to be brought.

sentences.t: فَغَابَ سَاعَةً وَحَضَرَ وَمَعَهُ جَارِيَةٌ رَشِيقَةُ الْقَدِّ بَارِزَةُ النَّهْدِ بِطَرْفٍ كَحِيلٍ وَخَلَاخِيلَ وَخَصْرٍ نَحِيلٍ وَرِدْفٍ ثَقِيلٍ
sentences.tr: fa-ghāba sāʿatan wa-ḥaḍara wa-maʿahu jāriyatun rashīqatu al-qaddi bārizatu al-nahdi bi-ṭarfin kaḥīlin wa-khalākhīla wa-khaṣrin naḥīlin wa-ridfin thaqīlin
sentences.l: So he was gone an hour and came, and with him a slave-girl, slender-of-the-stature, prominent-of-the-breast, with a kohl-darkened glance, and anklets, and a slim waist, and a heavy hip.
sentences.i: He was gone an hour and came back with a slave-girl, slender of figure and high of breast, with kohl-dark eyes, anklets, a slim waist and heavy hips.
sentences.n: Sajʿ: القد / النهد, then كحيل / خلاخيل / نحيل / ثقيل all rhyme in -īl. The string of nouns after بِـ ('with') is all genitive: they describe what she has, so the series runs on into the clause that follows. طرف is literally 'glance' or 'eye'; كحيل is 'kohl-darkened'.

sentences.t: وَثِيَابٍ أَحْسَنَ مَا يَكُونُ مِنَ الثِّيَابِ وَرُضَابٍ أَحْلَى مِنَ الْجُلَّابِ وَقَوَامٍ أَعْدَلَ مِنَ الْغُصُونِ الْمَائِلَةِ وَكَلَامٍ أَرَقَّ مِنْ نَسِيمِ الْأَسْحَارِ
sentences.tr: wa-thiyābin aḥsana mā yakūnu mina al-thiyābi wa-ruḍābin aḥlā mina al-julābi wa-qawāmin aʿdala mina al-ghuṣūni al-māʾilati wa-kalāmin araqqa min nasīmi al-asḥāri
sentences.l: and garments, the fairest that can be of garments, and sweet saliva sweeter than julep, and a figure more upright than the bending branches, and speech finer than the breeze of the dawns.
sentences.i: dressed in the finest clothes that could be, with lips sweeter than rose-syrup, a figure straighter than swaying branches, and speech softer than the breeze at daybreak.
sentences.n: Still the same list of what she comes 'with'. أحسن ما يكون من الثياب is a superlative idiom, 'the finest of clothes that there could be'. رضاب is the sweet moisture of the mouth; جلاب is julep, a sweet rose-water drink. Sajʿ again: الثياب / الجلاب, then الغصون المائلة / نسيم الاسحار.

sentences.t: كَمَا قَالَ فِيهَا بَعْضُ وَاصِفِيهَا شِعْرٌ ————————ر
sentences.tr: kamā qāla fīhā baʿḍu wāṣifīhā shiʿrun
sentences.l: as some of her describers said of her: verse
sentences.i: as one of her admirers has said of her, in verse:
sentences.n: The print introduces the poem with the word شعر and a ruled line ending in a lone ر; the mark is the print's own and is left standing as printed. It is not part of the poem; it may be a metre or rhyme sign.

sentences.t:
عَجِيبَةُ حُسْنٍ وَجْهُهَا بَدْرُ كَوْكَبِ * عَزِيزَةُ قَوْمٍ مِنْ زَبِيبٍ وَرَبْرَبِ
عَطَاهَا اِلَهُ الْعَرْشِ عِزّاً وَرِفْعَةً * وَظَرْفاً وَمَعْنًى ثُمَّ قَدّاً مُقْضَبِ
لَهَا فِي سَمَاءِ الْوَجْهِ سَبْعُ كَوَاكِبَ * عَلَى الْخَدِّ حُرَّاسٌ عَلَى كُلِّ مَرْقَبِ
اِذَا رَامَ اِنْسَانٌ يُسَارِقُ نَظْرَةً * شَيَاطِينُ لَفْظٍ اَحْرَقَتْهُ بِكَوْكَبِ
sentences.tr:
ʿajībatu ḥusnin wajhuhā badru kawkabin * ʿazīzatu qawmin min zabībin wa-rabrabi
ʿaṭāhā ilāhu al-ʿarshi ʿizzan wa-rifʿatan * wa-ẓarfan wa-maʿnan thumma qaddan muqḍabi
lahā fī samāʾi al-wajhi sabʿu kawākibin * ʿalā al-khaddi ḥurrāsun ʿalā kulli marqabi
idhā rāma insānun yusāriqu naẓratan * shayāṭīnu lafẓin aḥraqathu bi-kawkabi
sentences.i:
A marvel of beauty, her face the full moon among the stars, * a cherished lady of the folk of Zabīb and Rabrab;
the Lord of the Throne gave her glory and loftiness, * charm and meaning, and a stature slender as a cut branch.
Seven stars shine for her in the sky of her face, * guards upon her cheek, at every watch-post:
if any man sets out to steal a glance, * demons of speech burn him with a shooting star.
sentences.n: Verse, copied as pointed in the print. زبيب and ربرب are obscure here: ربرب is a herd of wild cattle (a common image for lovely women), زبيب 'raisins' and also a name; I take the pair as the name of her people or tribe, but this is uncertain. The seven 'stars' on her face stand guard over her cheek as the stars guard heaven, and burn eavesdropping devils with meteors (compare Qurʾān 72:8–9); لفظ 'speech' is odd in the last line, and لحظ 'glance' would suit the sense, but I follow the print. اِلَهُ is printed with short i and no long ā; read ilāhu. The kasra of مُقْضَبِ is for the rhyme.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا رَآهَا الْوَزِيرَا عَجَّبَتْهُ غَايَةَ الْعَجَبِ ثُمَّ الْتَفَتَ إِلَى السِّمْسَارِ وَقَٰلَ لَهُ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā raʾāhā al-wazīrā ʿajjabathu ghāyata al-ʿajabi thumma iltafata ilā al-simsāri wa-qāla lahu
sentences.l: And when he saw her, the vizier, she astonished him to the utmost of astonishment; then he turned to the broker and said to him:
sentences.i: When the vizier saw her, she filled him with wonder, and he turned to the broker and said,
sentences.n: الوزيرا is printed with a stray final alif (it recurs below); I vocalise it as it stands, as the subject. عجبته is read as the second-form 'astonished him'; the usual word would be أعجبته 'pleased him', which has an alif the print lacks. غاية العجب, 'the utmost of wonder', intensifies. قل is قال again.

sentences.t: كَمْ ثَمَنُ هَذِهِ الْجَارِيَةِ
sentences.tr: kam thamanu hādhihi al-jāriyati
sentences.l: How much is the price of this slave-girl?
sentences.i: "How much is this girl?"

sentences.t: فَقَالَ وَقَفَ سِعْرُهَا عَلَى عَشَرَةِ آلَافِ دِينَارٍ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla waqafa siʿruhā ʿalā ʿasharati ālāfi dīnārin
sentences.l: So he said: her price has stood upon ten of thousands of dinars.
sentences.i: He said, "Her price stands at ten thousand dinars."
sentences.n: وقف على, 'to stand at', is used of a price that has settled at a figure. 'Ten thousand' is built as 'ten (of) thousands'.

sentences.t: وَحَلَفَ صَاحِبُهَا أَنَّ الْعَشَرَةَ آلَافِ دِينَارٍ لَمْ تَجِيْ ثَمَنَ الْفَرَا رِبْحَ الَّتِي أَكَلَتْهَا وَلَا الشُّرْبِ وَلَا الْخِلَعِ الَّتِي خَلَعَتْهَا عَلَى مُعَلِّمِيهَا
sentences.tr: wa-ḥalafa ṣāḥibuhā anna al-ʿasharata ālāfi dīnārin lam tajī thamana al-farā ribḥa allatī akalathā wa-lā al-shurbi wa-lā al-khilaʿi allatī khalaʿathā ʿalā muʿallimīhā
sentences.l: And her owner swore that the ten of thousands of dinars did not come to the price of the farā, the gain of what she ate, nor the drink, nor the robes of honor that she bestowed upon her teachers,
sentences.i: and her owner swore that ten thousand dinars would not cover what she had eaten, nor her drink, nor the robes of honor she had given her teachers,
sentences.n: Obscure: ثمن الفرا ربح التي اكلتها. The sense is plainly 'the cost of her keep', but الفرا is hard: it may be a slip for القِرى 'provisions, guest-fare', or the farāʾ ('wild ass', as in the proverb), and ربح is 'profit', here 'worth'. I have pointed the letters as they stand and translated by the sense. لم تجي keeps the mark the print puts on the ي: it is the verb 'to come' (come to, amount to) in a Middle Arabic form with the ي kept. خلع على is 'to bestow a robe of honor on'.

sentences.t: فَإِنَّهَا تَعَلَّمَتِ الْخَطَّ وَالنَّحْوَ اللُّغَةَ وَالتَّفْسِيرَ وَأُصُولَ الْفِقْهِ وَالدِّينَ وَالطِّبَّ وَالتَّقْوِيمَ وَالضَّرْبَ بِالْآلَاتِ الْمُطْرِبَةِ
sentences.tr: fa-innahā taʿallamati al-khaṭṭa wa-al-naḥwa al-lughata wa-al-tafsīra wa-uṣūla al-fiqhi wa-al-dīna wa-al-ṭibba wa-al-taqwīma wa-al-ḍarba bi-al-ālāti al-muṭribati
sentences.l: for she learned the script, and the grammar, the language, and the commentary, and the roots of jurisprudence, and religion, and medicine, and the calendar, and the striking with the instruments, the delight-making ones.
sentences.i: for she has learned penmanship, grammar, philology, Qurʾānic commentary, the principles of jurisprudence, religion, medicine, astronomical reckoning, and the playing of instruments that gladden the heart.
sentences.n: اللغة has no wa- before it in the print; it stands beside النحو, 'grammar, (and) lexicography'. التفسير is commentary on the Qurʾān, أصول الفقه the 'roots' (sources and method) of jurisprudence, التقويم calendar and astronomical calculation. الضرب بـ, 'striking with', is playing an instrument; المطربة are those that move one to delight.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ الْوَزِيرُ عَلَيَّ بِسَيِّدِهَا فَأَحْضَرَهُ فِى الْوَقْتِ وَالسَّاعَةِ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla al-wazīru ʿalayya bi-sayyidihā fa-aḥḍarahu fī al-waqti wa-al-sāʿati
sentences.l: So the vizier said: Upon me, with her master! So he brought him, in the time and the hour.
sentences.i: The vizier said, "Bring her master to me!" and he was fetched on the spot.
sentences.n: فاحضره has no stated subject (the broker or an attendant). في الوقت والساعة, 'in the time and the hour', means at that very moment. The print writes في with a dotless ى, here and below; the pointing follows it.

sentences.t: فَإِذَا هُوَ رَجُلٌ عَجَمِيٌّ قَدْ أَبْقَى مَا أَبْقَى وَعَارَكَهُ الدَّهْرُ وَاسْتَبْقَى
sentences.tr: fa-idhā huwa rajulun ʿajamiyyun qad abqā mā abqā wa-ʿārakahu al-dahru wa-istabqā
sentences.l: And behold, he was a man, a Persian; he had left what he left, and Time had grappled with him and spared (him).
sentences.i: And there he was, a Persian, worn away by the years, with only what Time had spared of him, for Time had wrestled him down and let him live.
sentences.n: عجمي is any non-Arab, here a Persian. قد ابقى ما ابقى is an idiom of what is left over: the years had left of him only what they left, which is little. The subject of ابقى is not stated (the man, or Time); the second verb عاركه 'wrestled with him, rubbed him hard' has Time as subject. I read it as Time throughout.

sentences.t: كَمَا قَالَ الشَّاعِرُ شِعْرٌ ————————ز
sentences.tr: kamā qāla al-shāʿiru shiʿrun
sentences.l: as the poet said: verse
sentences.i: as the poet says:
sentences.n: The print's ruled line and lone letter, now ز, are left standing as before.

sentences.t:
اَرْ عَشَنِي الدَّهْرُ اَيْ رَعْشٍ * وَالدَّهْرُ ذُو قُوَّةٍ وَبَطْشِ
قَدْ كُنْتُ اَمْشِي وَلَسْتُ اَعْيَى * وَالْيَوْمَ اَعْيَى وَلَسْتُ اَمْشِي
sentences.tr:
ar ʿashanī al-dahru ayya raʿshin * wa-al-dahru dhū quwwatin wa-baṭshin
qad kuntu amshī wa-lastu aʿyā * wa-al-yawma aʿyā wa-lastu amshī
sentences.l:
Time made-me-tremble — what a trembling! * and Time is possessor of strength and violence;
I used to walk and was not weary * and today I am weary and I am not walking.
sentences.i:
Time has set me trembling, and how! * for Time has strength and a heavy hand.
I used to walk and never tire; * today I tire, and cannot walk.
sentences.n: Verse, copied as pointed in the print. The print has a space in ار عشني ('made me tremble'), which is kept; ارعشني is meant. أيّ رعش 'what a trembling' is an exclamation. The lines match the Persian's old age.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ لَهُ الْوَزِيرَا رَضِيتَ أَنْ تَأْخُذَ فِي هَذِهِ الْجَارِيَةِ عَشَرَةَ آلَافِ دِينَارٍ مِنَ السُّلْطَانِ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ سُلَيْمَانَ الزَّيْنِيِّ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla lahu al-wazīrā raḍīta an taʾkhudha fī hādhihi al-jāriyati ʿasharata ālāfi dīnārin mina al-sulṭāni Muḥammadi ibni Sulaymāna al-Zayniyyi
sentences.l: So he said to him, the vizier: Are you content to take, for this slave-girl, ten of thousands of dinars from the sultan Muḥammad son-of-Sulaymān al-Zaynī?
sentences.i: Then the vizier said to him, "Are you content to take ten thousand dinars for this girl from Sultan Muḥammad ibn Sulaymān al-Zaynī?"
sentences.n: رضيت is a question with the interrogative particle left out. في هذه الجارية is 'for this girl' (fī of price). The sultan named is the vizier's own master; الزيني is a family or title name.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ الْعَجَمِيُّ وَاللَّهِ لَقَدْ قَدَّ مْتُهَا لِلسُّلْطَانِ بِلَا شَيٍ كَانَ وَ احِبًا عَلَّيَ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla al-ʿajamiyyu wa-Allāhi laqad qaddamtuhā li-al-sulṭāni bi-lā shayʾin kāna wājiban ʿalayya
sentences.l: So the Persian said: By God, I presented her to the sultan with no-thing — it was incumbent upon me.
sentences.i: The Persian said, "By God, I had already offered her to the Sultan for nothing, as my duty required."
sentences.n: The print has several slips here. قد متها is قدمتها, 'I presented her', with a stray space; و احبا is واجبا, 'incumbent', also spaced and with ح for ج; شي is شيء without its hamza (the print marks it with a kasratan); and علّي puts the shadda on the lam instead of the ي. I keep the print's spaces and marks, point the letters as they stand, and read قدمتها, واجبا and عليّ by the sense.

sentences.t: فَعِنْدَ ذَلِكَ أَمَرَالْوَزِيرُ بِإِحْضَارِ الْأَمْوَالِ فَأُحْضِرَتْ فَوُزِنَتْ لِلْعَجَمِيِّ
sentences.tr: fa-ʿinda dhālika amara al-wazīru bi-iḥḍāri al-amwāli fa-uḥḍirat fa-wuzinat li-al-ʿajamiyyi
sentences.l: So at that, the vizier commanded the bringing of the monies; so they were brought, so they were weighed out for the Persian.
sentences.i: At that the vizier ordered the money to be brought; it was brought and weighed out for the Persian.
sentences.n: امرالوزير is printed as one word, 'the vizier commanded'; read with the break between the verb and its subject. أمر بـ, 'command (the doing of)', takes بِـ. The money is weighed because dinars were weighed out in the old coinage.

sentences.t: وَأَقْبَلَ النَّخَّاسُ عَلَى الْوَزِيرِ وَقَالَ عَنْ إِذْنِ مَوْلَانَا الْوَزِيرِ أَتَكَلَّمُ
sentences.tr: wa-aqbala al-nakhkhāsu ʿalā al-wazīri wa-qāla ʿan idhni mawlānā al-wazīri atakallamu
sentences.l: And the slave-dealer turned toward the vizier and said: On the permission of our master the vizier, I speak.
sentences.i: The slave-dealer turned to the vizier and said, "With our lord the vizier's leave, may I speak?"
sentences.n: النخاس is the slave-dealer, the same man as the broker above. عن اذن, 'on the permission of', is the courteous formula; the plain present أتكلم, 'I speak', serves as a request.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ الْوَزِيرُ هَاتِ مَا عِنْدَكَ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla al-wazīru hāti mā ʿindaka
sentences.l: So the vizier said: Give what is with you.
sentences.i: The vizier said, "Out with what you have to say."

sentences.t: فَقَالَ أَنَّ الرَّأْيَ عِنْدِي أَنْ لَاتَطْلَعَ بِهَذِهِ الْجَارِيَةِ لِلسُّلْطَانِ فِي هَذَا الْيَوْمِ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla anna al-raʾya ʿindī an lātaṭlaʿa bi-hādhihi al-jāriyati li-al-sulṭāni fī hādhā al-yawmi
sentences.l: So he said: that the opinion with me is that you not go up with this slave-girl to the sultan on this day,
sentences.i: He said, "My counsel is that you not take this girl up to the Sultan today,
sentences.n: أن after قال introduces the speech, as a quotation mark. لاتطلع is printed run together (lā taṭlaʿ). طلع بـ, 'go up with', is to take someone up to the palace.

sentences.t: فَإِنَّهَا قَادِمَةٌ مِنَ السَّفَرِ وَاخْتَلَفَ عَلَيْهَا الْهَوَى وَدَعَكَهَا السَّفَرُ
sentences.tr: fa-innahā qādimatun mina al-safari wa-ikhtalafa ʿalayhā al-hawā wa-daʿakahā al-safaru
sentences.l: for she is arriving from the journey, and the air has varied upon her, and the travel has rubbed her hard.
sentences.i: for she has just come from a journey, the air has changed on her, and the road has worn her down.
sentences.n: الهوى here is the 'air' or climate (not 'passion'); اختلف عليها is 'disagreed with her', so that a change of air has upset her. دعك is 'to knead, rub hard'.

sentences.t: وَلَكِنْ خَلِّهَا عِنْدَكَ فِي الْقَصْرِ عَشَرَةَ أَيَّامٍ لَمَّاتُرَدَّ إِلَى حَالِهَا
sentences.tr: wa-lākin khallihā ʿindaka fī al-qaṣri ʿasharata ayyāmin lammāturadda ilā ḥālihā
sentences.l: But leave her with you in the palace ten days, until she is returned to her condition,
sentences.i: but keep her with you in the palace for ten days, until she is restored to herself;
sentences.n: لماترد is printed run together. I read لمّا تُرَدّ 'until she is brought back' (passive); li-mā 'so that she be brought back' is also possible, and the sense is the same.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ أَدْخِلْهَا الْحَمَّامَ وَأَلْبِسْهَا أَحْسَنَ الثِّيَابِ وَاطْلَعْ بِهَا إِلَى السُّلْطَانِ
sentences.tr: thumma adkhilhā al-ḥammāma wa-albishā aḥsana al-thiyābi wa-iṭlaʿ bihā ilā al-sulṭāni
sentences.l: then make her enter the bath, and clothe her in the fairest of garments, and go up with her to the sultan,
sentences.i: then send her into the bath, dress her in the finest clothes, and take her up to the Sultan,

sentences.t: فَيَكُونَ لَكَ فِي ذَلِكَ الْحَظُّ الْأَوْفَرُ
sentences.tr: fa-yakūna laka fī dhālika al-ḥaẓẓu al-awfaru
sentences.l: so that there will be for you in that the share, the more abundant.
sentences.i: and you will have the richest share of the reward in it."
sentences.n: فيكون after a string of commands is 'and so there will be'.

sentences.t: فَتَأَمَّلَ الْوَزِيرُ كَلَامَ النَّخَّاسِ فَوَجَدَهُ صَوَابًا
sentences.tr: fa-taʾammala al-wazīru kalāma al-nakhkhāsi fa-wajadahu ṣawāban
sentences.l: So the vizier considered the speech of the slave-dealer and found it right.
sentences.i: The vizier weighed the slave-dealer's words and found them sound.

sentences.t: فَأَتَى بِهَا إِلَى قَصْرِهِ وَأَخْلَى لَهَا مَقْصُورَةً وَرَتَّبَ لَهَا كُلَّ يَوْمٍ مَا تَحْتَاجُ إِلَيْهِ مِنْ طَعَامٍ وَشَرَابٍ وَغَيْرِهِ فَمَكَثَتْ مُدَّةً عَلَى ذَلِكَ
sentences.tr: fa-atā bihā ilā qaṣrihi wa-akhlā lahā maqṣūratan wa-rattaba lahā kulla yawmin mā taḥtāju ilayhi min ṭaʿāmin wa-sharābin wa-ghayrihi fa-makathat muddatan ʿalā dhālika
sentences.l: So he came with her to his palace, and vacated for her an apartment, and appointed for her every day what she needed of it — of food and drink and other than it; and she stayed a while upon that.
sentences.i: He brought her to his palace, cleared a private apartment for her, and appointed for each day all that she needed of food, drink and the rest; and so she stayed for a time.
sentences.n: أتى بـ is 'to bring' (the verb chooses the بِـ). مقصورة is a closed-off chamber, a private apartment. Note ما تحتاج إليه, 'what she needs of it', where the pronoun repeats the object of إلى.

sentences.t: وَكَانَ لِلْوَزِيرِ الْفَضْلِ بْنِ خَاقَانَ وَلَدٌ كَأَنَّهُ الْبَدْرُ إِذَا بَدَرَ بِوَجْهٍ أَقْمَرَ وَخَدٍّ أَحْمَرَ عَلَيْهِ خَالٌ كَنُقْطَةِ عَنْبَرٍ بِعِذَارٍ أَخْضَرَ
sentences.tr: wa-kāna li-al-wazīri al-Faḍli ibni khāqāna waladun ka-annahu al-badru idhā badara bi-wajhin aqmara wa-khaddin aḥmara ʿalayhi khālun ka-nuqṭati ʿanbarin bi-ʿidhārin akhḍara
sentences.l: And there was to the vizier al-Faḍl son-of-Khāqān a son, as though he were the full moon when it bursts forth, with a face moon-bright, and a cheek red, upon it a mole like a dot of ambergris, with a down-line green.
sentences.i: Now the vizier al-Faḍl ibn Khāqān had a son, like the full moon when it bursts forth, with a moon-bright face and a rosy cheek, upon which lay a mole like a dot of ambergris, and a green down along the cheek.
sentences.n: Sajʿ: أقمر / أحمر / أخضر. بدر, 'to burst forth', is a pun on البدر 'the full moon'. The mole (خال) is dark as ambergris; عذار is the first growth of beard along the cheek, called 'green' for its dark fresh colour.

sentences.t: كَمَا قَالَ فِيهِ الشَّاعِرُ وَلَاقَصْرَ شِعْرٌ
sentences.tr: kamā qāla fīhi al-shāʿiru wa-lāqaṣra shiʿrun
sentences.l: as the poet said of him, and no shortfall: verse
sentences.i: as the poet says of him, and with nothing held back:
sentences.n: ولاقصر is printed as one word. I read it 'and no shortfall', a tag of full praise; this is uncertain, and a different word-division is possible.

sentences.t:
قَمَرٌ يَفْتِكُ بِاللَّوَاحِظِ اِنْ رَنَا * غُصْنٌ يُفَتِّتُ بِالْقِوَامِ اِذَا اْنْثَنَى
زَنْجِيُّ اللَّوَائِبِ عَسْجَدِيُّ لَوْنُهُ * حُلْوُ الشَّمَائِلِ قَدُّهُ يَحْكِي الْقَنَا
يَا قَبْلَهُ الْقَاسِي وَرِقَّةَ خَصْرِهِ * هَلَّا نُقِلْتَ اِلَى هُنَا مِنْ هَهُنَا
لَوْ كَانَ رِقَّةُ خَصْرِهِ فِي قَلْبِهِ * مَا جَارَ قَطُّ عَلَى الْمُحِبِّ وَلَا جَنَا
يَا عَاذِلِي فِي حُبِّهِ كُنْ عَاذِرِي * مَنْ لِي بِجِسْمٍ قَدْ تَمَلَّكَهُ الضَّنَى
مَا الذَّنْبُ اِلَّا لِلْفُوَادِ وَنَاظِرِي * فَدَعِ الْمَلَامَ وَخَلِّنِي فِي ذَا الْعَنَا
sentences.tr:
qamarun yaftiku bi-al-lawāḥiẓi in ranā * ghuṣnun yufattitu bi-al-qawāmi idhā inthanā
zanjiyyu al-lawāʾibi ʿasjadiyyu lawnuhu * ḥulwu al-shamāʾili qadduhu yaḥkī al-qanā
yā qablahu al-qāsī wa-riqqata khaṣrihi * hallā nuqilta ilā hunā min hahunā
law kāna riqqatu khaṣrihi fī qalbihi * mā jāra qaṭṭu ʿalā al-muḥibbi wa-lā janā
yā ʿādhilī fī ḥubbihi kun ʿādhirī * man lī bi-jismin qad tamallakahu al-ḍanā
mā al-dhanbu illā li-al-fuwādi wa-nāẓirī * fa-daʿi al-malāma wa-khallinī fī dhā al-ʿanā
sentences.i:
A moon that slays with glances when he gazes, * a branch that shatters hearts with his bearing when he sways,
dark-locked as a Zanjī, golden of hue, * sweet of nature, his figure like a lance.
O his hard heart! O slenderness of his waist, * why were you not moved from there to here?
If the slenderness of his waist were in his heart, * he would never have wronged a lover or done him harm.
O you who blame me for loving him, be my excuser: * who will help me, a body that wasting has taken for its own?
The fault lies only with my heart and my eye, * so leave off your blame and leave me in this affliction.
sentences.n: Verse, copied as pointed in the print. In line 3 the print has قَبْلَهُ ('before him'), evidently a slip for قَلْبَهُ 'his heart': the conceit is that the softness of his waist should move up into his heart; I translate by the sense. زنجي اللوائب is obscure: اللوائب is not a word I can place, and ذوائب 'locks' would suit; Zanjī is 'black like the Zanj'. القنا are lances, the stock image for an upright slender figure. The mark on the alif of اْنْثَنَى is the print's own.

sentences.t: وَكَانَ الصَّبِيُّ مَا عَرَفَ قَضِيَّةَ هَذِهِ الْجَارِيَةِ وَكَانَ وَالِدُهُ أَوْصَاهَا
sentences.tr: wa-kāna al-ṣabiyyu mā ʿarafa qaḍiyyata hādhihi al-jāriyati wa-kāna wāladuhu awṣāhā
sentences.l: And the-youth was (one who) had-not known the-affair of-this the-slave-girl, and his-father had charged her,
sentences.i: Now the youth did not know the story of this slave-girl, for his father had given her a charge.
sentences.n: كان + a perfect (كَانَ ... مَا عَرَفَ) is a past-perfect, “had not known”. The youth is Nūr al-Dīn ʿAlī, son of the vizier.

sentences.t: وَقَالَ لَهَا يَا بِنْتِي اعْلَمِي أَنِّي مَا اشْتَرَيْتُكِ إِلَّا سَرِيَّةً لِلْمَلِكِ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ سُلَيْمَانَ الزَّيْنِيِّ
sentences.tr: wa-qāla lahā yā bintī iʿlamī annī mā ishtaraytuki illā sariyyatan li-al-maliki Muḥammadi bni Sulaymāna al-Zaynī
sentences.l: and he-said to-her: O my-daughter, know that-I not I-bought-you except (as) a-concubine for-the-king Muḥammad son-of Sulayman al-Zayni,
sentences.i: and he said to her, “My daughter, know that I bought you only as a concubine for King Muḥammad ibn Sulaymān al-Zaynī,
sentences.n: ما ... إلا is the common “not ... except” for “only”. In the print سرية carries its shadda and kasra; they are kept as printed. A سُرِّيَّة (sarriyya) is a concubine.

sentences.t: وَأَنَّ لِي وَلَدًا مَا خَلَى بِصَبِيَّةٍ فِي الْحَارَةِ إِلَّا فَعَلَ بِهَا
sentences.tr: wa-anna lī waladan mā khalā bi-ṣabiyyatin fī al-ḥārati illā faʿala bihā
sentences.l: and that to-me (is) a-son (who) not has-been-alone with-a-girl in the-quarter except he-did to-her.
sentences.i: and I have a son who has never been alone with a girl in the quarter without having his way with her.
sentences.n: خلا بـ means “to be alone with”. The speaker plainly means that the boy takes every girl he can get; the verb فعل بها, “did to her”, is the blunt word for sexual use.

sentences.t: فَاجْعَلِي بَالَكِ مِنْهُ وَاحْذَرِي أَنْ تُرْبِهِ وَجْهَكِ أَوْ تُسْمِعِيهِ كَلَامَكِ
sentences.tr: fa-ijʿalī bālaki minhu wa-iḥdharī an turbihi wajhaki aw tusmiʿīhi kalāmaki
sentences.l: So make your-mind (turned) from-him, and beware that you-show-him your-face or you-make-him-hear your-speech.
sentences.i: So be on your guard against him, and take care never to show him your face or let him hear your voice.
sentences.n: جعل باله من is a colloquial idiom, “to be wary of”, literally “to put one’s mind on”. The print has تربه with a ب where تريه, “you show him”, is meant; it is pointed as printed. Note the second-person feminine endings: ـي and ـكِ.

sentences.t: فَقَالَتْ لَهُ الْجَارِيَةُ السَّمْعُ وَالطَّاعَةُ ثُمَّ تَرَكَهَا وَانْصَرَفَ
sentences.tr: fa-qālat lahu al-jāriyatu al-samʿu wa-al-ṭāʿatu thumma tarakahā wa-inṣarafa
sentences.l: And the-slave-girl said to-him: The-hearing and-the-obedience! Then he-left her and-went-away.
sentences.i: The slave-girl said to him, “With hearing and obedience.” Then he left her and went away.
sentences.n: السمع والطاعة is an elliptical reply, “(it is) hearing and obedience”, the stock answer of a servant to a command; it recurs many times.

sentences.t: فَاتَّفَقَ بِالْأَمْرِ الْمُقَدَّرَأَنَّ الْجَارِيَةَ فِي يَوْمٍ مِنَ الْأَيَّامِ دَخَلَتِ الْحَمَّامَ الَّذِي فِى الْمَنْزِلِ وَقَدْ غَسَلَهَا بَعْضُ الْجَوَارِي وَلَبِسَتِ الثِّيَابَ الْفَاخِرَةَ فَتَزَايَدَ حُسْنُهَا وَجَمَالُهَا
sentences.tr: fa-ittafaqa bi-al-amri al-muqaddara anna al-jāriyata fī yawmin mina al-ayyāmi dakhalati al-ḥammāma alladhī fī al-manzili wa-qad ghasalahā baʿḍu al-jawārī wa-labisati al-thiyāba al-fākhirata fa-tazāyada ḥusnuhā wa-jamāluhā
sentences.l: So it-so-fell-out by the-matter, the-decreed, that the-slave-girl on a-day of the-days entered the-bath which (is) in the-house, and some of-the-slave-girls had-washed her, and-she-put-on the-clothes, the-splendid; so increased her-beauty and-her-grace.
sentences.i: By the decree of fate it so happened that one day the slave-girl went into the bath in the house; some of the maids had washed her and she had put on splendid clothes, so that her beauty and grace were all the greater.
sentences.n: In the print المقدر and أن are run together (المقدران), one word; it is read as المقدر أن and left joined. اتفق بـ is “it fell out by ...”; الأمر المقدر is the decree of destiny.

sentences.t: وَدَخَلَتْ عَلَى السِّتِّ زَوْجَةِ الْوَزِيرِ فَبَاسَتْ يَدَهَا
sentences.tr: wa-dakhalat ʿalā al-sitti zawjati al-wazīri fa-bāsat yadahā
sentences.l: And she-entered upon the-lady, the-wife of-the-vizier, and-kissed her-hand.
sentences.i: She went in to the lady, the vizier’s wife, and kissed her hand.
sentences.n: باس “he kissed” (from بوس) is colloquial; Classical would be قبّل. السِّتّ, “lady, mistress”, is the colloquial form of سيّدة.

sentences.t: فَقَالَتْ لَهَا نَعِيمٌ يَا أَنِيسَ الْجَلِيسِ أَيْشْ حُسْنُ هَذَا الْحَمَّامِ
sentences.tr: fa-qālat lahā naʿīmun yā Anīsa al-Jalīsi aysh ḥusnu hādhā al-ḥammāmi
sentences.l: And-she-said to-her: Delight! O Anīs al-Jalīs, what (a) beauty (is) this the-bath!
sentences.i: She said to her, “Enjoy it, Anīs al-Jalīs! How lovely this bath is!”
sentences.n: نعيم is the courtesy said to someone fresh from the bath, “may it be a delight”. ايش is colloquial for أيّ شيء, “what?”, here exclamatory. Anīs al-Jalīs means “friend of the companion”; it is the slave-girl’s name.

sentences.t: فَقَالَتْ يَا سِتِّي مَا كُنْتُ مُحْتَاجَةً إِلَّا لِحُضُورِكِ فِيهِ
sentences.tr: fa-qālat yā sittī mā kuntu muḥtājatan illā li-ḥuḍūriki fīhi
sentences.l: And-she-said: O my-lady, not I-was needing (anything) except for-your-presence in-it.
sentences.i: She said, “My lady, I lacked nothing but your presence in it.”

sentences.t: فَعِنْدَ ذَلِكَ قَالَتِ السِّتُّ لِلْجَوَارِي قُومُوا بِنَا إِلَى الْحَمَّامِ
sentences.tr: fa-ʿinda dhālika qālati al-sittu li-al-jawārī qūmū binā ilā al-ḥammāmi
sentences.l: So at that said the-lady to-the-slave-girls: Rise with-us to the-bath.
sentences.i: Then the lady said to the maids, “Come with me to the bath.”
sentences.n: قوموا بنا, “rise with us”, is a way of saying “let us go”; the بـ is “with”. The recurring فعند ذلك is “thereupon”, literally “at that”.

sentences.t: قَالُوا سَمْعًا وَطَاعَةً وَنَهَضْنَ وَالسِّتُّ بَيْنَهُنَّ
sentences.tr: qālū samʿan wa-ṭāʿatan wa-nahaḍna wa-al-sittu baynahunna
sentences.l: They-said (masc.): Hearing and-obedience! and they-rose (fem.), and the-lady among-them (fem.).
sentences.i: “With hearing and obedience,” they said, and they rose, the lady in their midst.
sentences.n: The print gives the maids a masculine plural verb (قالوا) and then, a word later, a feminine one (نهضن): a Middle Arabic looseness, left as printed.

sentences.t: وَقَدْ وَكَّلَتْ بِبَابِ الْمَقْصُورَةِ الَّتِي فِيهَا أَنِيسُ الْجَلِيسِ جَارِيَتَيْنِ صَغِيرَتَيْنِ وَقَالَتْ لَهُمَا لَا تُمَكِّنَا أَحَدًا يَدْخُلُ لِلْجَارِيَةِ
sentences.tr: wa-qad wakkalat bi-bābi al-maqṣūrati allatī fīhā Anīsu al-Jalīsi jāriyatayni ṣaghīratayni wa-qālat lahumā lā tumakkinā aḥadan yadkhulu li-al-jāriyati
sentences.l: And she-had appointed over the-door of-the-chamber in-which (was) Anīs al-Jalīs two-slave-girls, two-small, and-said to-the-two: Do-not (you two) empower anyone (that) he-enters to-the-slave-girl.
sentences.i: She had set two young maids to guard the door of the chamber in which Anīs al-Jalīs was, and had told them, “Let no one go in to the girl.”
sentences.n: وكّل بـ is “to put (someone) in charge of”; the verb chooses the بـ. The print marks the shadda on تمكّنا (“do not give leave to”); it is kept. المقصورة is a closed chamber or private room. يدخل stands for أن يدخل, “that he enter”, with no particle.

sentences.t: فَقَالَتَا السَّمْعُ وَالطَّاعَةُ
sentences.tr: fa-qālatā al-samʿu wa-al-ṭāʿatu
sentences.l: And the-two-said: The-hearing and-the-obedience!
sentences.i: “With hearing and obedience,” they said.

sentences.t: فَبَيْنَمَا أَنِيسُ الْجَلِيسِ قَاعِدَةٌ بِالْمَقْصُورَةِ وَإِذَا بِابْنِ الْوَزِيرِ الَّذِي هُوَ نُورُالدِّينِ عَلِيٌّ قَدْ دَخَلَ وَسَأَلَ عَنْ أُمِّهِ وَعَنِ الْعَائِلَةِ
sentences.tr: fa-baynamā Anīsu al-Jalīsi qāʿidatun bi-al-maqṣūrati wa-idhā bi-ibni al-wazīri alladhī huwa Nūru al-Dīni ʿAlīyun qad dakhala wa-saʾala ʿan ummihi wa-ʿani al-ʿāʾilati
sentences.l: And-while Anīs al-Jalīs (was) sitting in-the-chamber, and-lo, the-son of-the-vizier, who (is) Nūr al-Dīn ʿAlī, had entered and-asked about his-mother and-about the-household.
sentences.i: While Anīs al-Jalīs sat in the chamber, behold, the vizier’s son, Nūr al-Dīn ʿAlī, came in and asked after his mother and the household.
sentences.n: بينما ... وإذا is the classic “while ... suddenly”; the بـ after إذا only marks what appears (here the vizier’s son). In the print نور الدين is run together as one word, نورالدين, here and elsewhere; it is left joined.

sentences.t: فَقَالَتْ لَهُ الْجَارِيَتَانِ دَخَلْنَ الْحَمَّامَ
sentences.tr: fa-qālat lahu al-jāriyatāni dakhalna al-ḥammāma
sentences.l: And said to-him the-two-slave-girls (nom. dual): They-entered (fem. pl.) the-bath.
sentences.i: The two maids said to him, “They have gone into the bath.”
sentences.n: The verb is singular feminine (قالت) before a dual subject: Middle Arabic agreement, vocalised as printed.

sentences.t: وَقَدْ سَمِعَتِ الْجَارِيَةُ أَنِيسُ الْجَلِيسِ كَلَامَ نُورِالدِّينِ عَلِيٍّ ابْنِ الْوَزِيرِ وَهِيَ مِنْ دَاخِلِ الْمَقْصُورَةِ فَقَالَتْ فِي نَفْسِهَا
sentences.tr: wa-qad samiʿati al-jāriyatu Anīsu al-Jalīsi kalāma Nūri al-Dīni ʿAlīyin ibni al-wazīri wa-hiya min dākhili al-maqṣūrati fa-qālat fī nafsihā
sentences.l: And the-slave-girl Anīs al-Jalīs had heard the-speech of-Nūr al-Dīn ʿAlī, the-son of-the-vizier, while she (was) from inside the-chamber, and-she-said in herself:
sentences.i: Now the slave-girl Anīs al-Jalīs had heard the words of Nūr al-Dīn ʿAlī, the vizier’s son, from inside the chamber, and she said to herself,

sentences.t: يَا تُرَى مَاشَأْنُ هَذَا الصَّبِيِّ الَّذِي قَالَ لِى الْوَزِيرُ عَنْهُ أَنَّهُ مَا خَلىَّ بِصَبِيَّةٍ فِى الْحَارَةِ إِلَّا فَعَلَ بِهَا وَاللَّهِ إِنِّي أَشْتَهِي أَنْ أَنْظُرَهُ
sentences.tr: yā tarā mā shaʾnu hādhā al-ṣabiyyi alladhī qāla lī al-wazīru ʿanhu annahu mā khallā bi-ṣabiyyatin fī al-ḥārati illā faʿala bihā wa-Allāhi innī ashtahī an anẓurahu
sentences.l: O (would I) see! what (is) the-affair of-this the-youth of-whom said to-me the-vizier about-him that-he not has-been-alone with-a-girl in the-quarter except he-did to-her; and-by-God, indeed-I desire that I-look-at-him.
sentences.i: “I wonder what sort of youth this is, of whom the vizier told me that he never was alone with a girl in the quarter without having his way with her. By God, I long to see him!”
sentences.n: يا ترى is a colloquial “I wonder”. ماشان is printed as one word, ما شأن, “what is the affair of”. The print’s خلّى here has its shadda on the ى (kept as printed); the sense is the same as خلا بـ above, “was alone with”. Nothing in the Arabic softens the sequel: أشتهي is “I desire”, and she goes to look.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ إِنَّهَا نَهَضَتْ عَلَى قَدَمَيْهَا وَهِيَ مِنْ أَثَرِ الْحَمَّامِ وَتَقَدَّمَتْ جِهَةَ بَابِ الْمَقْصُورَةِ وَنَظَرَتْ إِلَى نُورِالدِّينِ عَلِيٍّ
sentences.tr: thumma innahā nahaḍat ʿalā qadamayhā wa-hiya min athari al-ḥammāmi wa-taqaddamat jihata bābi al-maqṣūrati wa-naẓarat ilā Nūri al-Dīni ʿAlīyin
sentences.l: Then indeed-she rose on her-two-feet, and she (was) from the-trace of-the-bath, and-advanced (in the) direction of-the-door of-the-chamber and-looked at Nūr al-Dīn ʿAlī.
sentences.i: Then she rose to her feet, fresh from the bath, went forward toward the door of the chamber, and looked at Nūr al-Dīn ʿAlī.
sentences.n: من أثر الحمام is “from the bath’s trace”, that is, just out of the bath.

sentences.t: فَإِذَا هُوَ صَبِيٌّ كَالْبَدْرِ فِي تَمَامِهِ فَأَوْرَثَتْهَا النَّظْرَةُ أَلْفَ حَسْرَةٍ
sentences.tr: fa-idhā huwa ṣabiyyun ka-al-badri fī tamāmihi fa-awrathathā al-naẓratu alfa ḥasratin
sentences.l: And-lo, he (was) a-youth like-the-full-moon in its-completeness, and the-glance bequeathed-her a-thousand of-yearning-sighs.
sentences.i: And there he stood, a youth like the full moon in its perfection; and that one glance left her a thousand sighs of longing.
sentences.n: كالبدر في تمامه is the stock simile for beauty: the moon at the full. أورث is “to bequeath”: the glance leaves her a legacy of حسرة, the ache of longing and regret.

sentences.t: وَلَاحَتْ مِنَ الصَّبِيِّ الْتِفَاتَةٌ فَنَظَرَ الصَّبِيُّ إِلَيْهَا نَظْرَةً أَوْرَثَتْهُ أَلْفَ حَسْرَةٍ
sentences.tr: wa-lāḥat mina al-ṣabiyyi iltifātatun fa-naẓara al-ṣabiyyu ilayhā naẓratan awrathathu alfa ḥasratin
sentences.l: And a-turning-of-the-head showed from the-youth, and the-youth looked at-her a-glance (that) bequeathed-him a-thousand of-yearning-sighs.
sentences.i: Then the youth turned his head, and he looked at her, a look that left him a thousand sighs of longing.

sentences.t: وَوَقَعَ كُلٌّ مِنْهُمَا فِي شَرَكِ هَوَى الْآخَرِ
sentences.tr: wa-waqaʿa kullun minhumā fī sharaki hawā al-ākhari
sentences.l: And each of-the-two fell into the-snare of-the-love of-the-other.
sentences.i: And each of them fell into the snare of love for the other.

sentences.t: فَتَقَدَّمَ الصَّبِيُّ إِلَى الْجَارِيَتَيْنِ وَعَيَّطَ عَلَيْهِمَا فَهَرَبَتَا مِنْ بَيْنِ يَدَيْهِ
sentences.tr: fa-taqaddama al-ṣabiyyu ilā al-jāriyatayni wa-ʿayyaṭa ʿalayhimā fa-harabatā min bayni yadayhi
