sentences.l: So the-youth advanced to the-two-slave-girls and-shouted at-the-two, and-the-two-fled from between his-two-hands.
sentences.i: The youth went up to the two maids and shouted at them, and they fled from before him,
sentences.n: عيّط ʿalā, “to shout at”, is colloquial (Classical صاح). من بين يديه, “from between his hands”, is “from his presence”.

sentences.t: وَوَقَفَتَا مِنْ بَعِيدٍ تَنْظُرُ أَنَّهُ وَتَنْظُرُ أَنَّ مَا يَفْعَلُ
sentences.tr: wa-waqafatā min baʿīdin tanẓuru annahu wa-tanẓuru anna mā yafʿalu
sentences.l: and the-two-stood from afar, (she) looks that-he, and (she) looks that what he-does.
sentences.i: and stood at a distance, watching to see what he would do.
sentences.n: The print here reads تنظر انه وتنظر ان ما يفعل, with a singular verb after a dual subject, and the particles ان / انه look like a garbled تنظران ما يفعل, “the two watching what he does”. The pointing follows the letters as printed; the translation gives the evident sense.

sentences.t: وَإِذَا بِهِ تَقَدَّمَ إِلَى بَابِ الْمَقْصُورَةِ وَفَتَحَهُ وَدَخَلَ عَلَى الْجَارِيَةِ
sentences.tr: wa-idhā bihi taqaddama ilā bābi al-maqṣūrati wa-fataḥahu wa-dakhala ʿalā al-jāriyati
sentences.l: And-lo, with-him: he-advanced to the-door of-the-chamber and-opened it and-entered upon the-slave-girl.
sentences.i: And behold, he went up to the door of the chamber, opened it, and went in to the girl.
sentences.n: In وإذا به the بـ simply marks what appears, as above.

sentences.t: وَقَالَ لَهَا أَنْتِ الَّتِي اشْتَرَاكِ أَبِي لِي فَقَالَتْ لَهُ نَعَمْ
sentences.tr: wa-qāla lahā anti allatī ishtarāki abī lī fa-qālat lahu naʿam
sentences.l: and-said to-her: You (are) she-who my-father bought-you for-me? And-she-said to-him: Yes.
sentences.i: and said to her, “Are you the one my father bought for me?” and she said to him, “Yes.”

sentences.t: فَعِنْدَ ذَلِكَ تَقَلَّمَ الصَّبِيُّ إِلَيْهَا وَكَانَ فِي حَالِ السُّكْرِ وَأَخَذَ رِجْلَيْهَا وَعَمِلَهَا فِي وَسَطِهِ
sentences.tr: fa-ʿinda dhālika taqallama al-ṣabiyyu ilayhā wa-kāna fī ḥāli al-sukri wa-akhadha rijlayhā wa-ʿamilahā fī wasaṭihi
sentences.l: So at that the-youth advanced to-her, and-he-was in a-state of-the-drunkenness, and-took her-two-legs and-set her in his-middle.
sentences.i: Thereupon the youth came up to her — he was in a state of drunkenness — and took her by the legs and set her about his waist.
sentences.n: The print has تقلم, evidently a slip for تقدم, “advanced”; it is pointed as printed. وعملها في وسطه is literally “and made her in his middle”, that is, he settled her about his waist.

sentences.t: وَهِيَ شَبَّكَتْ يَدَيْهَا فِي عُنُقِهِ وَاسْتَقْبَلَتْهُ بِبَوْسٍ وَشَهِيقٍ وَغَنَجٍ وَمَصَّ لِسَانَهَا وَمَصَّتْ لِسَانَهُ وَأَزَالَ بَكَارَتَهَا
sentences.tr: wa-hiya shabbakat yadayhā fī ʿunuqihi wa-staqbalathu bi-bawsin wa-shahīqin wa-ghanajin wa-maṣṣa lisānahā wa-maṣṣat lisānahu wa-azāla bakāratahā
sentences.l: And she interlaced her-two-hands at his-neck and-received-him with-kissing and-sobbing-breath and-coquetry; and-he-sucked her-tongue and-she-sucked his-tongue, and-he-removed her-virginity.
sentences.i: She for her part clasped her hands behind his neck and met him with kisses, panting breaths, and coquettish languor; he sucked her tongue and she sucked his, and he took her maidenhead.
sentences.n: هي شبّكت, with the pronoun before the verb, is colloquial in word order. بوس is “kissing”, شهيق a drawn-in, gasping breath, غنج the languorous coquetry of a woman in love-play. Here and below the Arabic is explicit and the translation keeps it so.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا رَأَى الْجَارِيَتَانِ سَيِّدَ هُمَا الصَّغِيرَ دَخَلَ عَلَى الْجَارِيَةِ أَنِيسِ الْجَلِيسِ صَرَخَتَا وَعَيَّطَتَا
sentences.tr: fa-lammā raʾā al-jāriyatāni sayyida humā al-ṣaghīra dakhala ʿalā al-jāriyati Anīsi al-Jalīsi ṣarakhatā wa-ʿayyaṭatā
sentences.l: And-when the-two-slave-girls (nom.) saw their-master the-young (that he) had-entered upon the-slave-girl Anīs al-Jalīs, they-two-screamed and-they-two-shouted.
sentences.i: When the two maids saw their young master go in to the slave-girl Anīs al-Jalīs, they screamed and cried out.
sentences.n: The print leaves a space inside سيدهما, “their master”; it is kept as two words. الجاريتان is nominative where Classical has the accusative after رأى: it is left as printed.

sentences.t: وَكَانَ قَدْ قَضَى الصَّبِيُّ حَاجَتَهُ وَخَرَجَ هَارِبًا وَلِلنَّجَاةِ طَالِبًا وَفَرَّ مِنَ الْخَوْفِ عَقِبَ الْفِعْلِ الَّذِي فَعَلَهُ
sentences.tr: wa-kāna qad qaḍā al-ṣabiyyu ḥājatahu wa-kharaja hāriban wa-li-al-najāti ṭāliban wa-farra mina al-khawfi ʿaqiba al-fiʿli alladhī faʿalahu
sentences.l: And the-youth had already accomplished his-need and-went-out fleeing, and for-the-escape seeking, and-fled from the-fear in-the-wake-of the-deed which he-did.
sentences.i: The youth, having had his will, rushed out in flight, seeking only escape, and ran from fear in the wake of the deed he had done.
sentences.n: هاربًا ... طالبًا is a pair of rhyming participles (sajʿ). قضى حاجته is “he did his business” (here, he satisfied his desire).

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا سَمِعَتِ السِّتُّ عَيَاطَ الْجَارِيَتَيْنِ نَهَضَتْ وَخَرَجَتْ مِنَ الْحَمَّامِ وَالْعَرَقُ يَقْطُرُ مِنْهَا
sentences.tr: fa-lammā samiʿati al-sittu ʿayāṭa al-jāriyatayni nahaḍat wa-kharajat mina al-ḥammāmi wa-al-ʿaraqu yaqṭuru minhā
sentences.l: And-when the-lady heard the-shouting of-the-two-slave-girls, she-rose and-went-out from the-bath, and the-sweat dripping from-her.
sentences.i: When the lady heard the maids’ outcry she rose and came out of the bath with the sweat dripping from her.

sentences.t: وَقَالَتْ أَيْشْ هَذَا الْعَيَاطُ الَّذِي فِي الدَّارِ
sentences.tr: wa-qālat aysh hādhā al-ʿayāṭu alladhī fī al-dāri
sentences.l: And-she-said: What (is) this the-shouting which (is) in the-house?
sentences.i: and said, “What is this uproar in the house?”

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا قَرُبَتْ مِنَ الْجَارِيَتَيْنِ اللَّتَيْنِ كَانَتْ أَقْعَدَ تْهُمَا عَلَى بَابِ الْمَقْصُورَةِ قَالَتْ لَهُمَا وَيْلَكُمَا مَا الْخَبَرُ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā qarubat mina al-jāriyatayni allatayni kānat aqʿada tuhumā ʿalā bābi al-maqṣūrati qālat lahumā waylakumā mā al-khabaru
sentences.l: And-when she-drew-near to the-two-slave-girls, the-two-whom she-had seated-them-two at the-door of-the-chamber, she-said to-the-two: Woe-to-you-two! What (is) the-news?
sentences.i: When she came near the two maids whom she had seated at the door of the chamber, she said to them, “Woe to you! What is the matter?”
sentences.n: The print splits أقعدتهما as اقعد تهما; it is kept as two words. ويل plus a pronoun is a scolding exclamation, “woe to you”, not a curse; it recurs.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا رَأَتَاهَا قَالَتَاأَنَّ سَيِّدِي نُورَالدِّينِ جَاءَ إِلَيْنَا وَ ضَرَبَنَا فَهَرَبْنَا مِنْهُ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā raʾatāhā qālatā anna sayyidī Nūra al-Dīni jāʾa ilaynā wa-ḍarabanā fa-harabnā minhu
sentences.l: And-when the-two-saw her, the-two-said that my-lord Nūr al-Dīn came to-us and struck-us, so we-fled from-him.
sentences.i: When they saw her they said, “Our master Nūr al-Dīn came to us and beat us, and we ran away from him,
sentences.n: In the print قالتا and أن are run together (قالتاان), one word, left joined. The lone و before ضربنا is printed with a space after it; also kept.

sentences.t: فَدَخَلَ عَلَى أَنِيسِ الْجَلِيسِ وَعَانَقَهَا وَمَا نَدْرِي أَيْشْ عَمِلَ بَعْدَ ذَلِكَ
sentences.tr: fa-dakhala ʿalā Anīsi al-Jalīsi wa-ʿānaqahā wa-mā nadrī aysh ʿamila baʿda dhālika
sentences.l: and-he-entered upon Anīs al-Jalīs and-embraced-her, and-not we-know what he-did after that.
sentences.i: and he went in to Anīs al-Jalīs and embraced her, and we do not know what he did after that.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا صَيَّحْنَا عَلَيْكِ هَرَبَ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā ṣayyaḥnā ʿalayki haraba
sentences.l: But when we-cried-out upon-you, he-fled.
sentences.i: But when we cried out to you, he ran off.”
sentences.n: صيّح على, “to call out to”, is colloquial.

sentences.t: فَعِنْدَ ذَلِكَ تَقَدَّمَتِ السِّتُّ إِلَى أَنِيسِ الْجَلِيسِ وَقَالَتْ لَهَا مَا الْخَبَرُ
sentences.tr: fa-ʿinda dhālika taqaddamati al-sittu ilā Anīsi al-Jalīsi wa-qālat lahā mā al-khabaru
sentences.l: So at that the-lady advanced to Anīs al-Jalīs and-said to-her: What (is) the-news?
sentences.i: Thereupon the lady went up to Anīs al-Jalīs and said to her, “What has happened?”

sentences.t: فَقَالَتْ يَا سَيِّدَتِي أَنَا قَاعِدَةٌ وَإِذَا بِصَبِيٍّ جَمِيلٍ دَخَلَ عَلَيَّ وَقَالَ لِي أَنْتِ الَّذِي اشْتَرَاكِ أَبِي لِي فَقُلْتُ نَعَمْ
sentences.tr: fa-qālat yā sayyidatī anā qāʿidatun wa-idhā bi-ṣabiyyin jamīlin dakhala ʿalayya wa-qāla lī anti alladhī ishtarāki abī lī fa-qultu naʿam
sentences.l: And-she-said: O my-mistress, I (was) sitting, and-lo, a-youth, handsome, entered upon me and-said to-me: You (are) he-who my-father bought-you for-me? And-I-said: Yes.
sentences.i: She said, “My lady, I was sitting here when, behold, a handsome youth came in to me and said, ‘Are you the one my father bought for me?’ and I said, ‘Yes.’
sentences.n: أنتِ الذي uses the masculine relative for a woman, a Middle Arabic simplification; vocalised as printed.

sentences.t: وَاللَّهِ يَاسَيِّدَتِي اعْتَقَدْتُ أَنَّ كَلَامَهُ صَحِيحٌ فَعِنْدَ ذَلِكَ أَتَى عِنْدِي وَعَانَقَنِي
sentences.tr: wa-Allāhi yāsayyidatī iʿtaqadtu anna kalāmahu ṣaḥīḥun fa-ʿinda dhālika atā ʿindī wa-ʿānaqanī
sentences.l: By-God, O-my-mistress, I-believed that his-speech (was) true; so at that he-came to-me and-embraced-me.
sentences.i: By God, my lady, I thought what he said was true; so he came to me and embraced me.”
sentences.n: ياسيدتي is printed as one word.

sentences.t: فَقَالَتِ السِّتُّ كَلَّمَكِ شَيْئًا بِشَيٌ غَيْرَ ذَلِكَ
sentences.tr: fa-qālati al-sittu kallamaki shayʾan bi-shayʾun ghayra dhālika
sentences.l: And the-lady said: Did-he-speak-to-you a-thing, with a-thing other than that?
sentences.i: The lady said, “Did he say anything to you, or do anything, other than that?”
sentences.n: This question is obscure: the print has شيئا and then بشيٌ (with a tanwīn of damma printed on the ي, kept). I take it as “did he say something to you, (or do) something else besides that?”; the reading is uncertain.

sentences.t: قَالَتْ نَعَمْ وَأَخَذَ مِنِّي ثَلَٰثَ بَوْسَاتٍ
sentences.tr: qālat naʿam wa-akhadha minnī thalātha bawsātin
sentences.l: She-said: Yes, and-he-took from-me three kissings.
sentences.i: She said, “Yes, he took three kisses from me.”
sentences.n: ثلث is the print’s spelling of ثلاث; the dagger alif supplies the missing ā.

sentences.t: فَقَالَتْ مَا تَرَكَكِ مِنْ غَيْرِ افْتِضَاضٍ ثُمَّ بَكَتْ وَلَطَمَتْ وَجْهَهَا هِيَ وَالْجَوَارِي خَوْفَاعَلَى نُورِ الدِّينِ أَنْ يَذْبَحَهُ أَبُوهُ
sentences.tr: fa-qālat mā tarakaki min ghayri iftiḍāḍin thumma bakat wa-laṭamat wajhahā hiya wa-al-jawārī khawfan ʿalā Nūri al-Dīni an yadhbaḥahu abūhu
sentences.l: And-she-said: He-did-not-leave-you without deflowering. Then she-wept and-struck her-face, she and-the-slave-girls, fearing for Nūr al-Dīn that his-father slaughter-him.
sentences.i: The lady said, “He did not leave you without taking your maidenhead!” Then she wept and slapped her face, she and the maids, in fear for Nūr al-Dīn lest his father cut his throat.
sentences.n: In the print خوفا and على are run together (خوفاعلى), left joined. لطم وجهها, striking the face, is the conventional gesture of grief. افتضاض is the breaking of the hymen.

sentences.t: فَبَيْنَاهُمْ كَذَلِكَ وَإِذَا بِالْوَزِيرِ دَخَلَ وَسَأَلَ عَنِ الْخَبَرِ
sentences.tr: fa-baynāhum kadhālika wa-idhā bi-al-wazīri dakhala wa-saʾala ʿani al-khabari
sentences.l: And-while-they (were) thus, and-lo, the-vizier entered and-asked about the-news.
sentences.i: While they were so, behold, the vizier came in and asked what had happened.

sentences.t: فَقَالَتْ لَهُ زَوْجَتُهُ احْلِفْ أَنَّ مَا قُلْتُهُ لَكَ تَسْمَعُهُ قَالَ نَعَمْ
sentences.tr: fa-qālat lahu zawjatuhu iḥlif anna mā qultuhu laka tasmaʿuhu qāla naʿam
sentences.l: And-said to-him his-wife: Swear that what I-told to-you, you-will-hear-it. He-said: Yes.
sentences.i: His wife said to him, “Swear that you will hear out what I tell you.” He said, “Yes.”

sentences.t: فَمَا عَادَتْ عَلَيْهِ مَا فَعَلَهُ وَاللَّهِ فَحَزِنَ وَخَرَّقَ ثِيَابَهُ وَلَطَمَ وَجْهَهُ وَنَتَفَ لِحْيَتَهُ
sentences.tr: fa-mā ʿādat ʿalayhi mā faʿalahu wa-Allāhi fa-ḥazina wa-kharraqa thiyābahu wa-laṭama wajhahu wa-natafa liḥyatahu
sentences.l: And not she-returned upon-him what he-did, by-God! and-he-grieved and-tore his-clothes and-struck his-face and-plucked his-beard.
sentences.i: And she told him, by God, all that the boy had done; and he grieved, and tore his clothes, and slapped his face and plucked his beard.
sentences.n: This is uncertain. As printed, فما عادت عليه ما فعله would be “and she did not return upon him what he had done”; the sense required is that she recounted it, and I suspect فأعادت (“she related”) was meant. The translation follows the sense. Tearing clothes, striking the face and plucking the beard are the conventional signs of grief.

sentences.t: فَقَالَتْ لَهُ زَوْجَتُهُ لَا تَقْتُلْ نَفْسَكَ أَنَا أُعْطِيكَ مِنْ مَالِي عَشَرَةَ آلَافِ دِينَارٍ ثَمَنَهَا
sentences.tr: fa-qālat lahu zawjatuhu lā taqtul nafsaka anā uʿṭīka min mālī ʿasharata ālāfi dīnārin thamanahā
sentences.l: And said to-him his-wife: Do-not kill yourself; I will-give-you from my-wealth ten thousands of-dinar, her-price.
sentences.i: His wife said to him, “Do not kill yourself. I will give you ten thousand dinars from my own money as her price.”
sentences.n: The تمييز is “ten of thousands of dinars”; ثمنها, “her price”, stands in apposition.

sentences.t: فَعِنْدَ ذَلِكَ رَفَعَ رَأْسَهُ إِلَيْهَا وَقَالَ لَهَا وَيْلَكِ أَنَا مَا لِي حَاجَةٌ بِثَمَنِهَا وَلَكِنْ خَوْفِي أَنْ تَرُوحَ رُوحِي وَمَالِي
sentences.tr: fa-ʿinda dhālika rafaʿa raʾsahu ilayhā wa-qāla lahā waylaki anā mā lī ḥājatun bi-thamanihā wa-lākin khawfī an tarūḥa rūḥī wa-mālī
sentences.l: So at that he-raised his-head to-her and-said to-her: Woe-to-you! I — not to-me (is) a-need of-her-price, but my-fear (is) that there-go my-soul and-my-wealth.
sentences.i: At that he lifted his head to her and said, “Woe to you! I have no need of her price; what I fear is that my life and my wealth will go.”
sentences.n: حاجة بـ is “need of”, the بـ following the noun. The wordplay تروح روحي, “my soul goes”, from the same root ر-و-ح, is kept in the literal.

sentences.t: فَقَالَتْ لَهُ يَاسَيِّدِي وَكَيْفَ ذَلِكَ قَالَ لَهَا أَمَا تَعْلَمِينَ أَنَّ وَرَاءَنَا هَذَا الْعَدُوَّ الَّذِي يُقَالُ لَهُ الْمُعِينُ بْنُ سَاوَى وَمَتَى سَمِعَ بِهَذَا الْأَمْرِ تَقَدَّمَ إِلَى السُّلْطَانِ
sentences.tr: fa-qālat lahu yāsayyidī wa-kayfa dhālika qāla lahā amā taʿlamīna anna warāʾanā hādhā al-ʿaduwwa alladhī yuqālu lahu al-Muʿīnu ibnu Sāwā wa-matā samiʿa bi-hādhā al-amri taqaddama ilā al-sulṭāni
sentences.l: And-she-said to-him: O-my-lord, and how (is) that? He-said to-her: Do-you-not know that behind-us (is) this enemy, who is-said to-him al-Muʿīn son-of Sāwī, and-whenever he-hears of-this the-matter he-advances to the-sultan —
sentences.i: She said to him, “My lord, how so?” He said to her, “Do you not know that behind us stands that enemy of ours, called al-Muʿīn ibn Sāwī, and that as soon as he hears of this affair he will go before the Sultan —”
sentences.n: In the Nights al-Muʿīn ibn Sāwā is the vizier’s rival at court. سمع بـ is “to hear of”. The sentence is cut off by the end of the night.

sentences.t: وَأَدْرَكَ شَهْرَ زَادَ الصَّبَاحُ فَسَكَتَتْ
sentences.tr: wa-adraka Shahra Zāda al-ṣabāḥu fa-sakatat
sentences.l: And the-morning overtook Shahr Zad, and-she-fell-silent.
sentences.i: And the morning overtook Shahrazād, and she fell silent.
sentences.n: The print writes the name as two words, شهر زاد; they are kept apart.
